title: Alex Mukulu Laid to Rest with Official Funeral and Seven-Gun Salute
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Veteran playwright, actor and cultural icon Alex Mukulu was laid to rest on Thursday with an official state funeral, including a seven-gun salute, in recognition of his decades-long contribution to Uganda’s creative industry.
image_alt: Alex Mukulu funeral ceremony
content: Veteran playwright, actor, director and cultural icon Alex Mukulu was laid to rest on Thursday, 20 August 2026, at Kijabijo off the Gayaza–Kalagi road in a ceremony that marked a historic moment for Uganda’s creative industry. Mukulu, who died on 15 August at Kiruddu Hospital aged 72, was accorded an official burial by government — the first time a creative artist has received such recognition. He was survived by four children. President Yoweri Museveni hailed Mukulu as an icon whose death was a loss to Uganda’s theatre and culture. The President was represented at the burial by Minister of Gender, Labour and Social Development Lt Gen Henry Tumukunde. In a solemn ceremony attended by family, government officials, cultural figures and members of the creative fraternity, Mukulu was given a seven-gun salute. Soldiers observed traditional military protocol as the casket was lowered. In one of the most moving moments, Mukulu’s 10-string guitar was played for the last time before being placed in the grave with him. He had personally chosen the words for his epitaph: “My journey ends here. The remaining hills are yours to climb.” Musician and Senior Presidential Advisor on Creative Arts Eddy Kenzo described the state funeral as recognition of the value and dignity of Uganda’s creative industry, saying it gave artists renewed hope that their work matters. The burial followed a funeral service at St Paul’s Cathedral Namirembe and public viewing of the body at the National Theatre. Mukulu spent more than four decades using satire, comedy and drama to examine Uganda’s political and social realities. His work helped shape modern Ugandan theatre and inspired generations of artists. The official send-off signalled growing recognition of the creative sector’s contribution to national life. King Musah Media pays tribute to Alex Mukulu. May his soul rest in eternal peace.

title: Jambojet to Resume Nairobi–Entebbe Flights After Six-Year Break
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Kenyan low-cost carrier Jambojet will resume daily flights between Nairobi and Entebbe on 1 October 2026, ending a six-year absence from the Ugandan market
image_alt: Jambojet aircraft
content: Kenyan low-cost airline Jambojet will resume flights between Nairobi and Entebbe on 1 October 2026, returning to the Ugandan market after a six-year hiatus caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. The airline will operate a daily passenger service on the route, alongside cargo and parcel services. One-way fares are expected to start at approximately US$170. Jambojet Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director Karanja Ndegwa said the return forms part of the carrier’s strategy to strengthen regional connectivity and make air travel more accessible across East Africa. “Our return to Uganda is a strategic step forward in our mission to strengthen regional connectivity. We see significant opportunities to support business, tourism and trade between Kenya and Uganda,” Ndegwa said. The Nairobi–Entebbe corridor is projected to carry about 300,000 passengers in 2026. The service is also expected to give Ugandan travellers easier access to Kenya’s coastal destinations such as Mombasa, Diani, Malindi and Lamu. The announcement was made during a stakeholder engagement in Kampala attended by representatives from government, tourism, travel agencies and the business community. The Uganda Association of Travel Agents welcomed the return, noting growing momentum in regional travel and trade. Jambojet has expanded its fleet to 11 aircraft and recently marked carrying its 10 millionth passenger. The airline reported an on-time performance of 86.45 percent in July 2026. The resumption adds another option on a competitive route already served by Kenya Airways, Uganda Airlines and other carriers, potentially increasing choice and pressure on fares for travellers between the two East African capitals. King Musah Media will continue tracking developments in regional air connectivity.

title: Government Launches 100-Day Crackdown on Dangerous Taxis in Greater Kampala
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The Ministry of Works and Transport has launched a 100-day enforcement operation to remove taxis in dangerous mechanical condition from roads in the Greater Kampala Metropolitan Area. Police will begin impounding the vehicles from Monday.
image_alt: Dilapidated taxi on Kampala road
content: The government has ordered a 100-day crackdown on dilapidated and unroadworthy commuter taxis, commonly known as “Ganyegenya,” operating in the Greater Kampala Metropolitan Area. Minister for Works and Transport Fred Byamukama announced that police have been directed to impound taxis found in dangerous mechanical condition starting Monday, 24 August 2026. Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA) has provided a parking facility in Nakawa for the seized vehicles. The operation, dubbed Operation Ganyegenya, targets 14-seater taxis with serious defects including faulty brakes, worn-out tyres, defective steering, weakened chassis, malfunctioning lights, doors held by ropes or glue, and torn seats. “We cannot continue putting people’s lives at risk at the expense of votes or strikes,” Byamukama said. He warned that threats of industrial action or political consequences would not deter enforcement. The Minister noted that voluntary inspections conducted over the past 60 days found that none of the tested vehicles met roadworthiness standards. He clarified that well-maintained taxis, including newer models, will not be affected. The first phase covers Greater Kampala, including Kampala, Wakiso and surrounding areas, before potential extension to other parts of the country. Key routes mentioned include Katooke Road in Nansana, Gganda-Kyebando, Kalerwe-Gayaza, Nakawa-Luzira and others. Some taxi industry leaders have welcomed the move, saying it will protect passengers and responsible operators. Authorities insist the operation is not a ban on the taxi business but a safety measure to remove vehicles that present an unacceptable danger. Public transport safety remains a long-standing concern in the capital. Whether the 100-day operation delivers lasting change will depend on consistent enforcement and the availability of safer alternatives for both operators and commuters. King Musah Media will monitor the implementation of the crackdown

title: Long-Serving Principal of Hillside Schools Naalya Passes Away After Collapsing During Medical Check-Up
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Dr Henry Stanley Okia, the long-serving principal of Hillside Schools Naalya and a respected educationist with more than 40 years of service, has died. He collapsed while at a hospital for a medical check-up.
image_alt: Dr Henry Stanley Okia
content: The education community is mourning the death of Dr Henry Stanley Okia, the long-serving principal of Hillside Schools Naalya, who passed away on Thursday, 20 August 2026. Dr Okia collapsed at a medical facility where he had gone for a heart-related check-up. He was later pronounced dead at Case Hospital in Kampala. He had earlier been diagnosed with diabetes and was reported to have experienced some heart-related issues. He had appeared in high spirits just days earlier during the school’s Cultural Day on 15 August. Dr Okia’s career in education spanned more than four decades. He began teaching in the early 1980s after training at Namutamba Primary Teachers’ College in Mityana District. He taught at several schools, including Narambhai Road Primary School in Jinja and Nakasero Primary School in Kampala, before moving into private education. He served as head teacher at Lakeside Academy in Entebbe, helped establish Entebbe Junior School, and later joined Hillside Schools Naalya, where he led the nursery and primary sections for over two decades. In addition to his administrative role, Dr Okia earned a PhD in Education from Kyambogo University. His doctoral research focused on support supervision and teacher performance in government-aided primary schools in the Teso sub-region. Vice President Jessica Alupo was among those who paid tribute, recalling a recent discussion with him about establishing a school in Katakwi District. Parents, colleagues and former students have remembered him as an accessible, committed and mentoring leader. Burial arrangements are expected to be announced by the family and school management. King Musah Media extends heartfelt condolences to the family of Dr Henry Stanley Okia, the Hillside Schools community, and the wider education fraternity. May his soul rest in eternal peace.

title: Kenyan Mother Allegedly Stabs Five Children in Kampala, Two Dead
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: A 43-year-old Kenyan woman is under investigation after allegedly stabbing her five children at their home in Kalungu-Bunga, Makindye Division, Kampala, killing two and injuring three others.
image_alt: Police at the scene of the Bunga incident
content: Police are investigating a tragic domestic incident in which a Kenyan mother allegedly stabbed her five children at their home in Kalungu Zone, Bunga, Ggaba Parish, Makindye Division, early on Thursday, 20 August 2026. Two of the children died. Khadija Daizy, 14, was found dead in her bedroom. Her sister, Hawa Dalena, 7, later succumbed to her injuries at Nsambya Hospital. Three other siblings, aged 13, 8 and 5, survived with stab wounds and remain hospitalised. The suspect, identified as Dorothy Namayo, 43, a Kenyan national and mother of the victims, was also found injured at the scene. She is admitted at Mulago National Referral Hospital under police guard. According to Kampala Metropolitan Police Deputy Spokesperson ASP Luke Owoyesigyire, a housemaid was awakened around 4:00 a.m. by cries for help from the children. Upon opening the house, she discovered several children with severe stab wounds. During the incident, a Toyota Hiace van parked at the residence was set on fire and completely destroyed. Firefighters recovered a jerrycan suspected to have contained petrol. Police have registered cases of murder, attempted murder and arson at Kabalagala Police Station. Statements have been recorded from witnesses as investigations continue to establish the full circumstances and motive. Neighbours and the housemaid indicated that the attack followed ongoing domestic disputes between the woman and her husband, with some reports linking tensions to the husband’s alleged second marriage. Police have not yet confirmed the exact motive. The incident has left the community in shock. Authorities continue to provide medical care to the surviving children while the suspect remains under close guard. King Musah Media extends condolences to the family of the deceased children and hopes for the full recovery of the survivors.

title: Local Government Minister Uncovers Inflated Costs and Shoddy Work at Panyimur Health Centre III During Anti-Corruption Tour
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Minister of Local Government Balaam Barugahara was shocked during an inspection in Pakwach District after learning that a kitchen at Panyimur Health Centre III had cost Shs350 million amid other signs of poor workmanship and alleged mismanagement.
image_alt: Minister Balaam inspecting kitchen at Pakwach health centre
content: Minister of Local Government Balaam Barugahara has expressed shock at a kitchen constructed at Panyimur Health Centre III in Pakwach District that reportedly cost Shs350 million. The revelation came during the Minister’s ongoing “Expose the Corrupt” campaign inspections in the West Nile region. Leaders informed him of serious concerns surrounding a project valued at approximately Shs2.5 billion (some reports put the broader works at Shs2.9 billion) implemented under the Ministry of Health. According to local leaders, the newly constructed outpatient department has a collapsing ceiling, while cracks have developed in the latrine. Money intended for a perimeter fence was allegedly diverted to construct the kitchen, which itself developed cracks. Barugahara inspected the facility and viewed the kitchen that is said to have consumed Shs350 million. The quality of work was described as not matching the level of investment. The Minister’s visit also highlighted other irregularities in Pakwach, including a road project where nearly Shs900 million was reportedly spent on only about 10 metres of a planned one-kilometre low-cost surface road. Earlier related actions in the district saw the arrest of the Panyimur Town Clerk and engineers over shoddy road works. Barugahara directed further investigations into the health centre project by relevant anti-corruption agencies. The findings form part of a wider pattern the Minister has been exposing across multiple districts since taking office, ranging from ghost workers and inflated contracts to incomplete projects and diversion of public funds. A kitchen costing Shs350 million at a health centre while basic structures show early signs of failure raises serious questions about value for money, supervision and accountability in public construction projects. King Musah Media will continue following the investigations into the Pakwach projects and the broader anti-corruption campaign.

title: President Congratulates Officers for Contribution to Peace and Security, Advises Safe Investments
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Yoweri Museveni on Thursday presided over the retirement ceremony of 19 UPDF General Officers at State House, Entebbe. He congratulated them for their service and advised them on wise investment of their benefits.
image_alt: President Museveni with retiring UPDF Generals
content: President Yoweri Museveni, the Commander-in-Chief of the Uganda People’s Defence Forces, on Thursday, 20 August 2026, presided over the retirement ceremony of 19 General Officers at State House, Entebbe. The President congratulated the retiring officers for their contribution to the UPDF and the country, commending them for upholding discipline, patriotism, integrity and commitment to duty throughout their careers. “First of all, I congratulate the Generals for the great contribution they made to the UPDF. The UPDF and NRM have been able to build security,” Museveni said. He urged the retirees to remain committed to their families and communities and to use the experience gained during their military service to continue supporting society. The President specifically advised them to prioritise safe investments such as treasury bonds and fixed accounts that generate steady returns before venturing into capital-intensive businesses. Among those who retired are Gen Edward Katumba Wamala, Lt Gen Charles Otema Awany, Lt Gen Charles Angina, Maj Gen Abel Kandiho, Maj Gen Geoffrey Tumusiime Katsigazi, Maj Gen Apollo Kasiita Gowa and Maj Gen Leopold Kyanda, alongside 12 Brigadier Generals. Deputy Chief of Defence Forces Lt Gen Sam Okiding noted that the officers had made significant contributions to the transformation of the UPDF and the maintenance of peace and security. Defence and Veteran Affairs Minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka urged the retiring officers to continue serving the country as ambassadors of the UPDF even after leaving active service. The retirement of the 19 generals formed part of a larger send-off that saw a total of 1,817 officers and militants retire in August 2026. The ceremony marked the formal end of long and distinguished careers for some of the force’s most senior officers and the beginning of a new chapter of civilian life and continued national contribution. King Musah Media congratulates the retiring generals on their service to Uganda.

title: Five Kisoro District Officials Arrested Over Alleged Sale of Jobs
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The State House Anti-Corruption Unit, working with CID, has arrested five Kisoro District Local Government officials, including the District Speaker and the Chairperson of the District Service Commission, over allegations of selling jobs.
image_alt: Kisoro District officials under arrest
content: Five Kisoro District Local Government officials have been detained by the State House Anti-Corruption Unit in collaboration with the Criminal Investigations Directorate over allegations of soliciting and receiving money from job applicants in exchange for assistance in securing employment. Those arrested are District Speaker Hakizimana Amos, District Service Commission (DSC) Chairperson Nshaka Erastus, DSC Member Turamuhawe Richard, District Councillor Mfitumukiza John, and alleged broker Muhanika Alphonse. Two other suspects — DSC Secretary Francesca Mugisha and teacher-middleman Matata Alex — are still on the run. According to the Anti-Corruption Unit, preliminary findings indicate that between October and December 2025, the suspects, together with others still at large, allegedly solicited and received approximately UGX 200 million from various job applicants. Investigations are in advanced stages. Once completed, the suspects are expected to be charged before the Anti-Corruption Court with corruption-related offences. The Unit has appealed to members of the public who were asked to pay or who paid money in connection with securing jobs in Kisoro District to come forward and report additional cases. The arrests form part of the ongoing nationwide anti-corruption drive that has seen several local government officials detained in different districts over similar allegations of job racketeering and abuse of office. Selling public jobs remains one of the most corrosive forms of corruption, denying meritorious candidates opportunities and undermining confidence in local government institutions. King Musah Media will continue following the Kisoro investigations and related anti-corruption actions.

title: Cavendish University Graduates 1,059 Students at 15th Ceremony
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Cavendish University Uganda has graduated 1,059 students from 33 nationalities at its 15th graduation ceremony. Chancellor and former Nigerian President Goodluck Jonathan urged the Class of 2026 to focus on impact.
image_alt: Cavendish University 15th Graduation Ceremony
content: Cavendish University Uganda has conferred degrees and diplomas on 1,059 students drawn from 33 nationalities during its 15th graduation ceremony held at Speke Resort Munyonyo. The ceremony, held under the theme “Graduating Global Talent for Employment, Entrepreneurship and Impact,” celebrated the Class of 2026. Of the graduands, 703 received bachelor’s degrees, 285 earned master’s degrees, 61 graduated with diplomas and one received a certificate. The class comprised 577 male and 473 female students. Chancellor of the University and former President of Nigeria, H.E. Dr Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, challenged the graduates to look beyond titles and wealth and instead pursue meaningful impact. “Graduation is not merely a destination; it is a summit,” he said. He called on the Class of 2026 to be employable in skill, entrepreneurial in mindset and impactful in purpose, urging them to “go forth into the global arena.” Jonathan emphasised that a university qualification carries a responsibility to apply knowledge in service of humanity and to create meaningful change wherever graduates find themselves. Guest of Honour and Minister for Trade, Industry and Cooperatives Sanjay Gokaldas Tanna challenged the graduates to become problem-solvers and value creators rather than simply job seekers. Vice Chancellor Dr Olive Sabiiti noted the university’s growing international footprint and revealed that Cavendish had introduced a virtual graduation clearance system developed by its Registry and Information Technology departments. The ceremony marked another milestone for the private university as it continues to position itself as a regional hub for higher education with a focus on producing graduates ready for employment, entrepreneurship and societal contribution.
King Musah Media congratulates the Class of 2026 and Cavendish University Uganda on the successful 15th graduation ceremony.

title: UEDCL Under Fire Over Persistent Outages and Rising Losses Since Umeme Takeover
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Uganda Electricity Distribution Company Limited continues to face intense public and parliamentary criticism over frequent power outages, rising energy losses and slow connections since taking over from Umeme. Many customers say the situation has not improved and in some areas has worsened.
image_alt: Power lines and electricity infrastructure
content: More than a year after the government took over electricity distribution from Umeme Limited, Uganda Electricity Distribution Company Limited (UEDCL) remains under heavy fire from consumers, Members of Parliament and industry observers over persistent outages, rising losses and delayed service. Households and businesses across Kampala and other parts of the country continue to report frequent planned and unplanned blackouts. Social media is filled daily with complaints of power going off at predictable hours, sometimes for entire nights, and of the same areas being scheduled for shutdowns repeatedly even after earlier works were supposedly completed. UEDCL regularly issues notices of planned maintenance and technical faults, but many customers argue that the frequency and duration of interruptions have increased compared with the latter years of the Umeme concession. Response times to faults have also been a source of frustration. Parliamentary committees have put the company on the spot. Legislators have questioned why Ugandans are not seeing meaningful improvement despite the company receiving significant public funding and loans since the takeover. Energy losses have risen to about 18.5 percent from roughly 15 percent at the time of handover, well above the national target. Each percentage point of loss is estimated to cost millions of dollars annually. UEDCL officials have acknowledged challenges stemming from an ageing and overloaded network, rapid growth in demand, vandalism, transformer failures and a large backlog of customers who paid for connections but are still waiting. The company says it has upgraded hundreds of transformers, is implementing a multi-million-dollar investment plan and has improved some fault-resolution times in recent months. More than 200,000 paid-up customers remain in the connection backlog, largely due to meter supply issues. Leadership changes have also marked the period. Top managers were previously sent on forced leave or exited amid concerns over performance and workplace culture. The broader Energy ministry saw a change at the top, with a new minister appointed, yet many ordinary consumers say the quality of supply on the ground has not shifted significantly. The transition from a private concessionaire to full state management was sold on promises of greater investment, lower costs and better service. While UEDCL points to ongoing works and inherited infrastructure deficits, the gap between official explanations and the daily experience of repeated blackouts continues to fuel public anger. Reliable electricity is not a luxury. It underpins household life, small businesses, manufacturing and the wider economy. Until the frequency of outages drops, connections accelerate and losses are brought under control, confidence in the post-Umeme distribution arrangement will remain low. King Musah Media will continue tracking UEDCL’s performance and the government’s response to the growing service delivery concerns.

title: Balaam Calls for Tougher Anti-Corruption Measures in Local Governments
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Minister of Local Government Balaam Barugahara has called for stronger anti-corruption and accountability measures in local governments, warning that the loss of public funds is directly denying citizens essential services.
image_alt: Minister Balaam Barugahara speaking at an event
content: Minister of Local Government Balaam Barugahara has issued a strong call for tougher anti-corruption measures and tighter accountability systems in local governments, arguing that the misuse of public resources is crippling service delivery nationwide. Speaking while opening the Financial Year 2027/28 Programme Conditional Grants negotiations between the central government and local governments in Kampala, Balaam warned that every shilling lost to corruption is money that cannot build classrooms, support health facilities, maintain roads, provide clean water or strengthen productive communities. He cited poorly constructed facilities and inadequate sanitation infrastructure as clear examples of how weak oversight and graft undermine government programmes. The Minister urged local government leaders to strengthen procurement controls, financial management, monitoring, verification and accountability mechanisms. He also called for greater involvement of communities, journalists and local leaders in tracking government projects so that citizens know what is being implemented in their areas and can hold officials to account. Balaam specifically warned officials against bypassing established systems, referencing an incident in Mbarara where a town clerk allegedly took over procurement and payment functions after sidelining the procurement officer. He said such practices expose local governments to the abuse of public resources. The remarks come against the backdrop of an ongoing nationwide anti-corruption campaign led by the Minister and State Minister Justine Nameere. The drive has so far resulted in the interdiction, arrest or investigation of scores of local government officials across multiple districts over allegations ranging from ghost workers and inflated contracts to diversion of road funds, Parish Development Model resources and other public monies. Balaam challenged local governments to raise own-source revenue collections and prioritise capital development and agro-processing programmes capable of improving citizens’ livelihoods. While the campaign has drawn praise for spotlighting accountability gaps, its long-term success will depend on sustained investigations, successful prosecutions and systemic reforms that make the theft of public funds both difficult and costly. King Musah Media will continue following the anti-corruption efforts in local governments.

title: SC Villa Captain David Owori Beaten to Death by Robbers in Kampala
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: SC Villa captain and Uganda Cranes player David Owori has died after being brutally attacked by suspected robbers near his home in Makindye, Kampala. The 27-year-old was assaulted with paving stones after resisting the theft of his phone and belongings.
image_alt: David Owori in SC Villa colours
content: Uganda’s football community is mourning the death of SC Villa captain and national team player David Owori, who was fatally assaulted by suspected robbers outside his home in Makindye, Kampala. The 27-year-old, popularly known as Colgate, was attacked on the evening of 4 August 2026 as he approached his residence. Witnesses said a group of assailants struck him with paving stones after he resisted attempts to steal his mobile phone and other belongings. He was left unconscious at the scene. Owori was first rushed to a nearby medical facility before being transferred to Case Hospital for specialised care. He succumbed to severe head and brain injuries the following day. SC Villa described the loss as profound. “We have lost more than a player — we have lost a leader, brother and friend,” the club said in a statement. The club announced that his number 15 shirt would be retired in his honour. The Federation of Uganda Football Associations (FUFA) paid tribute to Owori as “a leader and an inspiration to a generation,” noting that the country had lost a son, a leader and a star. Owori was a versatile player who featured as a right-back and midfielder. He helped SC Villa secure a record 17th Uganda Premier League title in 2024 and had previous stints with Vipers SC as well as clubs in Spain and Sweden. He also earned caps for the Uganda Cranes. Kampala Metropolitan Police confirmed that detectives were following leads to identify and apprehend those responsible. The killing has reignited public concern over violent street crime in the capital, coming shortly after similar incidents involving other sports personalities. Parliament observed a moment of silence in Owori’s honour, while calls for swift justice continue from the football fraternity and the wider public. King Musah Media extends heartfelt condolences to the family, SC Villa, FUFA and all who knew David Owori. May his soul rest in peace.

title: Janet Museveni Joins President in Welcoming Bishop LaDonna Osborn at State House
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Yoweri Museveni and First Lady Janet Museveni on Wednesday hosted international evangelist Bishop Dr LaDonna C. Osborn at State House Entebbe ahead of the consecration of their daughter, Pastor Patience Rwabwogo.
image_alt: President and First Lady with Bishop LaDonna Osborn at State House
content: President Yoweri Museveni and First Lady and Minister of Education and Sports Janet Museveni on Wednesday, 19 August 2026, received international evangelist Bishop Dr LaDonna C. Osborn at State House Entebbe. The visit comes ahead of the scheduled consecration of their daughter, Pastor Patience Rwabwogo, as an Episcopal Bishop on 23 August. The engagement marked one of the First Lady’s more visible recent public appearances alongside the President. In a statement, President Museveni noted that Dr Osborn recalled her first visit to Uganda in 1985 with her late mother, who ministered in the country during a difficult period in its history. The First Lady also fondly remembered the late evangelist, who prayed with the Museveni family and gave their children their first Bibles. “We reflected on Uganda’s transformation over the years and the enduring friendship between the Osborn family and Uganda. I welcome Dr Osborn back to Uganda and wish Pastor Patience a blessed consecration,” the President wrote. Janet Museveni described the meeting as special and deeply nostalgic. She expressed gratitude for Dr Osborn’s continued love for Uganda and her support for Pastor Patience, praying that God would guide and strengthen her daughter in the new responsibility. The Osborn family’s connection to Uganda spans decades through Christian ministry. The upcoming consecration is expected to draw prominent religious and other figures. The State House meeting combined personal family history with the public milestone of Pastor Patience’s elevation in ministry. King Musah Media wishes Pastor Patience Rwabwogo well as she prepares for her consecration.

title: Muhoozi Represents Uganda at Gabon’s 66th Independence Celebrations
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba joined African heads of state in Gabon for the country’s 66th Independence Anniversary celebrations and held private talks with President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema.
image_alt: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba at Gabon Independence celebrations
content: Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, joined several African leaders in Libreville for celebrations marking Gabon’s 66th Independence Anniversary. Gen Kainerugaba attended the 17 August events at the invitation of Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, who also serves as the country’s supreme commander of defence and security forces. Upon arrival, the CDF was received by Gabon’s Minister of Defence, Brig Gen Brigitte Onkanowa, and the Chief of General Staff of the Gabonese Armed Forces, Gen Jean-Bédel Bouka. His delegation included State Minister for Agriculture Desire Muhooza, Maj Gen Henry Masiko and Brig Gen Wycliff Keita. After the independence parade and official ceremonies, Gen Kainerugaba held private talks with President Oligui Nguema. Details of the discussions were not publicly disclosed, but the visit is expected to advance cooperation in military collaboration and regional security. Other African leaders present included President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo, President Alassane Ouattara of Côte d’Ivoire, President Carlos Vila Nova of São Tomé and Príncipe, President Umaro Sissoco Embaló of Guinea-Bissau and President Adama Barrow of The Gambia. The celebrations commemorated Gabon’s independence from French colonial rule, achieved on 17 August 1960. A highlight included the inauguration of a monument dedicated to Georges Aleka Damas, composer of the national anthem. The visit builds on recent high-level contacts. President Oligui Nguema visited Uganda in August 2024 for talks with President Yoweri Museveni on trade, defence, tourism and health, and returned to Kampala in May 2026 for Museveni’s inauguration. Gen Kainerugaba’s presence in Libreville underscores Uganda’s continued efforts to expand strategic partnerships across the continent beyond its traditional East African focus. King Musah Media will continue tracking Uganda’s defence and diplomatic engagements.

title: Uganda Approves and Advances UPDF Deployment to Gaza Stabilisation Force
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Parliament has approved the deployment of a Uganda People’s Defence Forces contingent to the Gaza Strip as part of the proposed International Stabilisation Force. The move follows a request channelled through US President Donald Trump’s emissaries and is seen as carrying both security and diplomatic significance.
image_alt: UPDF soldiers on parade
content: Uganda has taken concrete steps toward deploying troops to the Gaza Strip after Parliament approved a government motion authorising a Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF) contingent to join the proposed International Stabilisation Force (ISF). The motion was tabled by Defence and Veteran Affairs Minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka and passed during a plenary sitting. The Minister told lawmakers that US President Donald Trump, through emissaries, had contacted President Yoweri Museveni in July seeking Uganda’s contribution to the multinational force envisioned under the US-backed Gaza stabilisation plan. “Following the invitation by His Excellency Donald Trump… the President of the Republic of Uganda is ready to deploy in the Gaza Strip the desired Uganda People’s Defence Forces contingent,” Kiwanuka stated. According to the government, the UPDF contingent would operate under strict principles of neutrality, comply with international humanitarian law, protect civilians without taking sides in political disputes, and function solely under the mandate of the stabilisation mission. Planning meetings have already been held between senior UPDF officers, US Embassy officials in Kampala and representatives of the proposed force. Some legislators raised concerns about the risks of deploying troops to a volatile environment and questioned the adequacy of preparation and legal arrangements. Government and UPDF representatives in the House defended the decision, citing Uganda’s track record in regional and international peace support operations and the country’s constitutional commitment to promoting international peace and security. Beyond the immediate security role, analysts and officials have linked the deployment to Uganda’s broader diplomatic ambitions, including its nomination of veteran diplomat Olara Otunnu for the position of United Nations Secretary-General. Participation is viewed in some quarters as a demonstration of willingness to shoulder international responsibilities. Recent reports indicate that Ugandan and Burundian military representatives have conducted pre-deployment site-related engagements, signalling that preparations are advancing even as the overall Gaza stabilisation framework continues to face political and operational hurdles. The decision places Uganda among a small group of countries that have publicly committed troops to the ISF. How the mission evolves, the exact size and role of the UPDF contingent, and the risks involved will remain matters of close public interest. King Musah Media will continue monitoring developments around the proposed deployment.

title: Museveni Proposes Tax Exemption for Health Workers as Cabinet Restores Intern Pay
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Yoweri Museveni has proposed exempting health workers’ salaries from tax, while Cabinet has restored equal monthly facilitation for all medical interns in the current cohort after weeks of controversy.
image_alt: Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi addressing Parliament
content: President Yoweri Museveni has proposed that salaries of medical workers should be exempted from tax, similar to the arrangement enjoyed by members of the security forces. Health Minister Dr Chris Baryomunsi disclosed the President’s guidance while briefing Parliament on Tuesday. He said the proposal will form part of a comprehensive health workforce paper that Cabinet has directed the Ministry to prepare. At the same sitting, Baryomunsi announced that Cabinet has suspended a controversial policy that sought to differentiate facilitation between government-sponsored and privately sponsored medical interns. All 2,490 interns in the current cohort, deployed across 77 accredited centres, will now receive the existing monthly facilitation of approximately Shs1.27 million (subject to tax), leaving them with a net of about Shs1 million. The earlier plan would have limited privately sponsored interns mainly to a meals allowance. “Cabinet recommended that we suspend that provision of facilitation for medical interns, meaning that we pay them as it has been,” Baryomunsi told MPs, drawing applause. The decision follows weeks of tension, protests and uncertainty among newly graduated health professionals who had resisted reporting for internship over the proposed changes. The Uganda Medical Association subsequently directed interns to report for duty after the government assurance. Cabinet has also dropped a proposal that would have required medical students to complete internship before graduating. Internship will remain a separate requirement for professional registration. Beyond the immediate intern issue, the Minister said government will review the broader challenge of absorbing the growing number of trained doctors and other health professionals into the public health system, including questions of how many the country needs to train and how their employment can be sustainably financed. The dual announcements — restoration of equal intern pay and the President’s tax exemption idea — come against the backdrop of persistent concerns about understaffing, low motivation and the loss of health workers to better-paying opportunities. Whether the tax proposal advances into actual policy will depend on further consultations and fiscal considerations. King Musah Media will continue following developments in the health sector workforce policy.

title: Museveni Grants Official Burial to Veteran Playwright Alex Mukulu
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Yoweri Museveni has granted an official burial to celebrated Ugandan playwright, actor and director Alex Mukulu, who died on 15 August at the age of 72. The burial is scheduled for 20 August in Kijabijjo, Gayaza.
image_alt: Alex Mukulu, the late veteran playwright
content: President Yoweri Museveni has granted an official burial to veteran playwright, actor, director and musician Alex Edward Kabangala Mukulu, who passed away on 15 August 2026 at the age of 72. The announcement was made by Minister for the Presidency Milly Babalanda, who said the National Organising Committee is already engaging with the bereaved family to organise a befitting send-off. “I wish to inform you that the President of the Republic of Uganda, H.E. Gen. Museveni, has granted an official burial to the fallen statesman, Mr Alex Edward Kabangala Mukulu. Accordingly, the N.O.C. is engaging with the bereaved family to organise a befitting send-off on August 20, 2026, in Kijabijjo, Gayaza,” Babalanda stated. Mukulu’s body was taken to the Uganda National Theatre for public viewing, where members of the arts fraternity, family and members of the public paid their last respects. A funeral service was also planned at Namirembe Cathedral before the burial at his ancestral home. Mukulu was widely regarded as one of Uganda’s most influential theatre practitioners. Over a career spanning more than four decades, he used satire, drama and music to examine political and social realities. His notable works include “30 Years of Bananas,” “Wounds of Africa,” “Guest of Honour,” “Muzukulu wa Kabangala” and “Journey to Self-Realization,” which was performed at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Kampala in 2007. The decision to accord him an official burial is recognition of his significant contribution to Uganda’s cultural and creative industry. Tributes from artists, cultural leaders and the public have continued to pour in since his death, describing him as a pioneer who shaped generations of performers. King Musah Media once again extends condolences to the family, friends and the entire creative fraternity. May his soul rest in eternal peace.

title: IGG Interdicts URSB Registrar General Mercy Kainobwisho and Three Senior Officials
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The Inspector General of Government has ordered the interdiction of Uganda Registration Services Bureau Registrar General Mercy Kainobwisho and three other senior officials. The move follows a presidential directive for an audit into alleged financial impropriety at the agency.
image_alt: URSB Registrar General Mercy Kainobwisho
content: The Inspector General of Government, Lady Justice Naluzze Aisha Batala, has ordered the immediate interdiction of Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB) Registrar General Mercy Kainobwisho and three other senior officials as investigations into alleged corruption and mismanagement intensify. The other officials interdicted are Deputy Registrar General Alex Aganya, Commissioner for ICT and Innovations Arthur Kwesiga, and Assistant Commissioner for Business Registration Services Walid Kule. The IGG directed Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Norbert Mao to effect the interdiction of Kainobwisho, while the URSB Board was instructed to interdict the three other officers. The action is intended to protect the integrity of ongoing investigations and prevent possible interference. The interdictions stem from a July 24 directive by President Yoweri Museveni ordering an audit into allegations of embezzlement of government funds, abuse of office, institutional mismanagement, money laundering and maladministration at URSB. The President directed the IGG to lead the probe with assistance from State House auditors. Minister Mao has since appointed Mustapher Ntale, the Deputy Registrar General in charge of Registries, as acting Registrar General until further notice. A planned residential executive training for URSB officials at the National Leadership Institute in Kyankwanzi was also halted. The allegations that triggered the presidential intervention were raised internally, including by Commissioner for Business Registration Gilbert Agaba, who cited inflated ICT contracts, irregular procurements, weak financial controls and other governance concerns. URSB has confirmed that an audit is underway in accordance with established procedures and that services to the public remain available. No findings have yet been publicly released, and the officials have not been declared guilty of any offence. Interdiction is an administrative measure pending the outcome of investigations. The developments at URSB, an agency responsible for critical business, property and intellectual property registrations, will be closely watched for both the integrity of the probe and continuity of service delivery. King Musah Media will continue following the investigations and any further official updates.

title: Besigye Treason Trial: Witness Reveals Spy Camera Hidden in Power Bank
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: A prosecution witness has told the High Court that a hidden camera inside a power bank was used to record meetings in which Dr Kizza Besigye allegedly discussed plans to acquire weapons and overthrow the government. The treason trial is proceeding with Besigye tried in absentia.
image_alt: High Court session in the Besigye treason trial
content: The High Court in Kampala has heard dramatic testimony in the treason trial of veteran opposition leader Dr Kizza Besigye, with the first prosecution witness detailing how a covert camera concealed in a mobile power bank was used to record alleged discussions about acquiring weapons and overthrowing the government. Andrew Wilson Orlando, a private security investigator, told Justice Emmanuel Baguma of the Criminal Division that he secretly recorded meetings involving Besigye and Joel Wakayima, a Ugandan based in Switzerland. Wilson said he had been approached by Wakayima to facilitate the supply of weapons — including hand grenades, drones and surface-to-air missiles — and to arrange paramilitary training for between 40 and 60 people. He told court that the discussions included alleged plans to attack Kampala and that Wakayima had proposed detonating a hand grenade at Café Javas along Acacia Avenue because government officials frequented the premises. According to the witness, some of the meetings took place at his apartment, where he used the hidden recording equipment. He also claimed the group discussed using drones and framing attacks on the Allied Democratic Forces. Besigye is being tried alongside Obeid Lutale and UPDF Captain Denis Oola on charges of treason and misprision of treason. The offences carry a maximum penalty of death upon conviction. All the accused deny the charges. Justice Baguma has ruled that the trial can proceed in Besigye’s absence after the court was informed that he had declined to attend despite being medically cleared as fit to stand trial. The testimony has intensified the high-stakes nature of a case that has already drawn significant public and political attention. For the State, the recordings and Wilson’s account form a central pillar of the prosecution. For Besigye’s supporters and legal team, the circumstances of the evidence-gathering and the decision to proceed in his absence raise serious questions about fairness and due process. The trial continues, with the court expected to hear further prosecution witnesses. King Musah Media will keep following the proceedings closely.

title: Deputy Speaker Commends Career of Integrity at Launch of Odongo’s Autobiography
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Deputy Speaker Thomas Tayebwa has described the career of UNEB Executive Director Dan Odongo as exemplary and one that should inspire public servants across Uganda. He spoke at the launch of Odongo’s book in Kampala.
image_alt: Deputy Speaker Thomas Tayebwa speaking at Dan Odongo’s book launch
content: Deputy Speaker of Parliament Thomas Tayebwa has praised the career of Uganda National Examinations Board (UNEB) Executive Director Dan Odongo, describing it as exemplary and worthy of emulation by public servants across the country. Tayebwa made the remarks on Friday evening while speaking at the launch of Odongo’s book, titled From Humble Beginnings: The Journey of a Teacher Who Rose to Lead a Nation’s Trust, held at Hotel Africana in Kampala. He said Odongo’s record at UNEB demonstrated what public service should truly be about. “Leadership is not about titles; it is about service, honesty, and commitment to the people one leads. A title may open the door, but only one’s actions earn lasting respect,” the Deputy Speaker stated. Odongo has led UNEB through several examination cycles and has been widely associated with efforts to maintain the integrity of national assessments. His journey from a classroom teacher to the helm of one of the country’s most sensitive public institutions forms the core of the newly launched autobiography. The book launch brought together education stakeholders, public officials and well-wishers who turned up to celebrate Odongo’s contribution to the education sector. In a public service environment often criticised for inefficiency and lack of accountability, recognition of long-serving officers who maintain professional standards carries particular weight. Tayebwa’s endorsement places emphasis on character and results over mere position. King Musah Media congratulates Dan Odongo on the launch of his book and on a career that has drawn national recognition.

title: Veteran Playwright and Actor Alex Mukulu Dies at 72
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Veteran Ugandan playwright, actor, musician and theatre director Alex Mukulu has died at the age of 72. His death has left the country’s creative industry in mourning.
image_alt: Veteran playwright and actor Alex Mukulu
content: Uganda’s arts community is mourning the death of veteran playwright, actor, musician and theatre director Alex Mukulu, who has passed away at the age of 72. The news, first reported by several media houses and confirmed across entertainment platforms on Saturday, 15 August 2026, has triggered an outpouring of tributes from artists, journalists and cultural enthusiasts. Born in 1954 in Misebe, Ssingo County in Buganda, Mukulu studied Film and Drama at Makerere University after attending Kololo Secondary School. He went on to become one of the most influential figures in Ugandan theatre over more than four decades. His best-known works include the plays “30 Years of Bananas,” “Wounds of Africa,” “Guest of Honour,” “Excuse Me Mzungu,” and “Journey to Self-Realization,” the latter performed at the opening of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Kampala in 2007. He was also a musician and composer whose work cut across political, social and cultural themes. Mukulu was widely respected for using theatre as a tool to mirror society, challenge power and reflect the lived experiences of ordinary Ugandans. In recent years he returned to the stage with productions that continued to spark conversation. Tributes have described him as a forefather of modern Ugandan theatre whose contribution paved the way for younger generations of actors, playwrights and performers. Many have hailed his creativity, courage and lasting impact on the country’s cultural landscape. Details regarding the cause of death and funeral arrangements had not been officially released by the time of this report. The loss of Alex Mukulu marks the end of an era in Ugandan performing arts. His body of work remains a significant part of the nation’s cultural heritage. King Musah Media joins the creative fraternity in mourning the veteran artiste and extends condolences to his family, friends and colleagues

title: King Saha Packs Kololo to Capacity at Tondeka E’Kololo Festival
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: King Saha has filled Kololo Airstrip to maximum capacity for his Tondeka E’Kololo Festival. Crowds poured in throughout the day, turning the venue into a vibrant sea of music, fashion and celebration.
image_alt: Massive crowd at King Saha’s Tondeka E’Kololo Festival
content: Musician King Saha has delivered one of the biggest turnouts of the year after packing Kololo Airstrip to capacity for his highly anticipated Tondeka E’Kololo Festival on Friday, 14 August 2026. From afternoon into the evening, revellers streamed into the venue in large numbers. Photos and videos circulating on social media show the grounds filled with fans dressed in their best, creating a colourful atmosphere of music, fashion and high energy. New Vision described the scene as Kololo having “surrendered” to King Saha, with the crowd behaving as if it was already midnight long before the main performance. The concert comes just three days after the singer was arrested in a dramatic raid on his Kyanja residence that involved reports of gunfire. He was later released. The successful turnout has been widely interpreted as a strong show of support from his fan base. Supporters waved flags and chanted as the energy built up. Some sections of the crowd were heard raising political slogans, reflecting the charged atmosphere that often accompanies major public gatherings in Uganda. Yet the dominant mood remained celebratory as fans turned up to enjoy the music. King Saha had spent the preceding days aggressively promoting the show, moving around Kampala and selling tickets. Ordinary tickets were priced at UGX 20,000 and VIP at UGX 50,000, with tables going for higher amounts. The heavy attendance suggests the marketing paid off and that the artiste retains significant pulling power in the industry. For Uganda’s entertainment scene, a sold-out or near-capacity show at Kololo remains a major achievement. Few local artistes consistently fill the historic airstrip. King Saha’s ability to draw such numbers so soon after a high-profile security incident underlines both his popularity and the resilience of his brand. As the night progressed, the focus stayed on the performance and the collective energy of thousands of fans who turned up to celebrate.

title: Court Delays Ruling as Prosecution Seeks to Block Live Coverage of Proceedings
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The bail hearing of NUP Deputy President for Buganda, Hon Muwanga Kivumbi, has been adjourned to 25 August 2026. The prosecution is also seeking to stop live coverage of the court proceedings.
image_alt: NUP leaders at Butambala Chief Magistrate’s Court
content: The bail hearing of National Unity Platform Deputy President for Buganda, Hon Muwanga Kivumbi, has been adjourned to 25 August 2026 by the Butambala Chief Magistrate’s Court. Kivumbi faces charges of inciting violence and managing an unlawful society. Leader of the Opposition Joel Ssenyonyi and NUP Acting President John Baptist Nambeshe, together with other party leaders, attended the session on Friday. Instead of proceeding to the merits of the bail application, the prosecution applied to stop the live coverage of the court proceedings. The court will rule on both the application to bar live streaming and the defence’s bail application on the next hearing date. Nambeshe described the prosecution’s move as a diversion from addressing the substance of the case. He said the party remains hopeful that justice will prevail and that Kivumbi will be granted his constitutional right to bail. The adjournment continues a pattern of delays in the matter. Kivumbi and his supporters maintain that the charges are politically motivated, while the State has insisted on prosecuting the case under the law. The right to bail is a constitutional entitlement, subject to the court’s assessment of whether the accused is likely to abscond, interfere with witnesses, or pose a threat to public order. Equally, the question of live coverage raises issues of open justice and public access to court proceedings in cases of significant public interest. How the court balances these competing considerations on 25 August will be closely watched by both political actors and advocates of judicial transparency.

title: Six New Power Lines Completed as MPs Decry Limited Electricity Access
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: State Minister for Energy Sidronius Okaasai has announced the completion of six of eleven pending power lines, delivering 141,400 new electricity connections. At the same time, Members of Parliament have raised a general outcry over limited connectivity across the country.
image_alt: State Minister Sidronius Okaasai addressing Parliament on rural electrification
content: State Minister for Energy Sidronius Okaasai has announced the completion of six of eleven pending power lines, delivering 141,400 new electricity connections. At the same time, Members of Parliament have raised a general outcry over limited connectivity across the country.  Story body:

The Ministry of Energy has completed and commissioned six of the eleven power lines that were still under construction when the Rural Electrification Agency was mainstreamed into the ministry. State Minister for Energy Sidronius Okaasai told Parliament that the completed projects have delivered 1,780.59 kilometres of medium-voltage lines, 2,646.53 kilometres of low-voltage lines and 981 transformers. The works have connected 141,400 new electricity consumers, with all planned connections under the project undertaken. However, the minister also laid bare the funding challenges inherited by the ministry. When REA was mainstreamed, the government took on about UGX 570 billion in obligations for ongoing rural electrification works. Over the last four years, only about UGX 222.07 billion has been received. The funding shortfall has left contractors and consultants unpaid and communities still awaiting compensation. One completed project alone requires UGX 38 billion to compensate affected persons. Government has increased the rural electrification budget from UGX 35 billion to UGX 161 billion in the current financial year. The ministry, however, says it needs about UGX 200 billion annually to clear the inherited obligations and finance new projects. Meanwhile, during plenary, Members of Parliament raised a general outcry over limited electricity connectivity across the country. Legislators pointed to persistent gaps in access that continue to affect households, businesses and social services in many constituencies. The simultaneous reporting of progress and parliamentary frustration underscores the scale of Uganda’s rural electrification challenge. While new lines and connections represent tangible expansion, the backlog of unpaid obligations and the continued complaints from MPs show that demand still far outstrips the pace of delivery. Reliable electricity remains central to household welfare, small business growth and the broader economic transformation agenda. Closing the gap will require consistent funding, faster project execution and clearer accountability for the resources already allocated. King Musah Media will continue following the implementation of rural electrification programmes and parliamentary oversight of the energy sector.

title: Masaka SS Student Raped and Strangled as Wave of Attacks on Young Women Sparks Alarm
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: A Senior Four student at Masaka Secondary School, Rayati Nassali Nakato, has been found dead after being raped and strangled. The killing forms part of a disturbing pattern of recent attacks on young women that has left many Ugandans demanding stronger protection and faster police action.
image_alt: Rayati Nassali Nakato, the Masaka SS student found dead
content: A Senior Four candidate at Masaka Secondary School has been raped and strangled to death in a case that has intensified public alarm over the safety of young women in Uganda. The victim, identified as Rayati Nassali Nakato, was reported missing before her body was discovered. Police and local reports indicate she was sexually assaulted and strangled with a rope. The killing comes amid a series of similar incidents reported within a short period. In the space of about one week, a young woman was raped, killed and dumped in an unfinished building in Nabingo along Bataka Lane. Another case involved a housemaid who was reportedly raped and murdered by thieves in Kyampisi-Kakoola, Mukono District. Journalist Gabriel Buule, who first highlighted the cluster of cases, wrote that the pattern raises urgent questions about the safety of girls and young women across the country. These incidents have triggered widespread public concern. Many Ugandans are asking why such brutal attacks continue and whether current policing and community protection measures are adequate. The cases have also revived conversations about personal safety, the risks young women face in both urban and peri-urban settings, and the need for faster, more visible investigations. Police have not yet issued a comprehensive public statement linking the cases or detailing arrests in all of them. Investigations into Nakato’s death and the other reported incidents remain ongoing. The deaths of young women in such violent circumstances demand more than expressions of shock. They require thorough, transparent investigations, swift arrests where evidence exists, and concrete steps to improve safety for girls and women in homes, schools, workplaces and public spaces. Families of the victims deserve justice. The wider public deserves assurance that the state takes the protection of its young citizens seriously. King Musah Media will continue following the police investigations and any official updates on these cases.

title: CDF Urges Regional Forces to End Dependence on Unpredictable External Support and Fully Fund Standby Force
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba has urged Eastern African countries to build military independence and reduce reliance on external support. He made the call while opening the 36th Ordinary Session of the Eastern Africa Standby Force in Kampala
image_alt: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba addressing EASF defence chiefs in Kampala
content: Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chairman of the Eastern Africa Standby Force (EASF) Chiefs of Defence and Security Committee, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, on Thursday opened the 36th Ordinary Session in Kampala with a strong call for regional strategic self-reliance. Addressing defence leaders from Eastern Africa, Gen Kainerugaba said shifting external support mechanisms demand internal funding and operational independence if the region is to secure its future. He pointed to the ongoing transition to the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) as a clear reminder that the region must remain ready for change. “The ongoing transition to the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia is a clear reminder that our region must remain ready for change. We cannot afford to depend on unpredictable circumstances. We must remain prepared to respond whenever the African Union and member states require collective action,” he stated. Gen Kainerugaba expressed optimism about the commitment of EASF member states but stressed that self-reliance must actively drive the region’s defence posture. He pledged that Uganda would fully meet its funding obligations to the Force. “Sustaining readiness, conducting exercises, and maintaining operational capability require resources that are often stretched. I would like to inform the director that we are going to fully meet our obligation in terms of funding,” the CDF said. He added that constrained resources should sharpen the resolve to find practical and lasting solutions. The Ugandan general noted that the Kampala meeting is taking place amid rapidly evolving threats. Conflicts are changing, extremist threats are evolving, illicit networks are becoming more sophisticated, and technology is reshaping how operations are planned and conducted. On readiness, he emphasised that preparedness is no longer measured by numbers alone. It is measured by agility, interoperability, foresight, and the ability to respond decisively under uncertain circumstances. Reflecting on the recent EASF Force Verification Exercise hosted in Uganda, Gen Kainerugaba said a standby force earns credibility not only through the missions it undertakes but through the confidence it inspires before deployment becomes necessary. “Preparedness cannot be improvised in crises. It must be built in advance, maintained consistently, and tested regularly,” he said. EASF Director Brig Gen Ronald Rwivanga of the Rwanda Defence Force commended Uganda’s leadership and noted progress under the Secretariat’s strategic plan. He highlighted that for the first time, seven partners had delivered their financial commitments on time. Uganda’s State Minister for Defence and Veteran Affairs (Defence), Hon Grace Akifeza Ngabirano, also expressed confidence in the EASF’s capacity and stressed that unified solidarity remains essential for lasting peace on the continent. The 36th Ordinary Session continues with closed-door discussions on operational deployment frameworks and the budget for the 2026–2027 fiscal year. The Eastern Africa Standby Force is mandated by the African Union to predict, prevent and respond to security crises, conflicts and humanitarian disasters in the region through rapid-deployment peace support operations. Its active member states include Burundi, Comoros, Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, Sudan and Uganda. The call for self-reliance comes at a time when external funding for African peace support missions has become less predictable. Whether member states will translate the rhetoric into consistent financial and operational commitments will determine the Force’s real effectiveness in the years ahead. King Musah Media will continue following the outcomes of the Kampala session.

title: 12th Parliament Holds Inaugural Service Led by Archbishop Kaziimba
author: Musanya Musa
excerpt: The Archbishop of the Church of Uganda, Dr Stephen Samuel Kaziimba Mugalu, has led the inaugural service for the 12th Parliament under the theme “Called to Serve.”
image_alt: Inaugural service of the 12th Parliament
content: The 12th Parliament of Uganda gathered on Thursday for its inaugural service led by the Archbishop of the Church of Uganda, the Most Rev Dr Stephen Samuel Kaziimba Mugalu. The service was held under the theme “Called to Serve.” It was attended by Deputy Speaker Thomas Tayebwa (Ruhinda North County), Leader of the Opposition Joel Ssenyonyi (Nakawa Division West), Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs Norbert Mao (Laroo-Pece Division), other ministers, Members of Parliament and staff of Parliament. The inaugural service marks a traditional moment of spiritual reflection as the new Parliament begins its work. King Musah Media will continue covering the proceedings of the 12th Parliament.

title: Armed Security Operatives Raid Musician’s Home with Reports of Gunfire Days Before Kololo Show
author: Musanya Musa
excerpt: Musician King Saha was arrested on Tuesday evening after armed security personnel raided his apartment in Kyanja. The operation, which involved reports of gunfire, came as he promoted his concert scheduled for 14 August at Kololo Airstrip.
image_alt: Musician King Saha, was arrested on 11 August 2026 during a security operation at his Kyanja residence while promoting his Tondeka E’Kololo Festival.
content: Ugandan musician King Saha (Mansur Semanda) was arrested on the evening of 11 August 2026 following a dramatic raid on his apartment in Kyanja. The singer had spent the day mobilising fans and selling tickets for his “Tondeka E’Kololo Festival” scheduled for Friday, 14 August at Kololo Airstrip. Ordinary tickets were priced at UGX 20,000 and VIP at UGX 50,000. According to eyewitness accounts and videos circulating on social media, armed security personnel — described by some as JATT operatives and military police — raided the residence. Reports indicated scenes of panic, gunfire, and at least one person injured in the leg. King Saha was held at gunpoint and taken away. NUP Secretary General David Lewis Rubongoya and other activists described the incident as a violent abduction and called for an end to impunity. Authorities had not issued a detailed public statement clarifying the reasons for the operation or any formal charges at the time of the initial reports. Later updates indicated that King Saha was released and visited injured members of his team. The raid, coming just three days before the scheduled performance, has raised questions about the status of the concert and the circumstances surrounding the security intervention. As of the latest information, the singer had been released. The full details of any injuries, the status of seized items, and whether the Kololo show will proceed as planned remain subject to official clarification.

title: Seventh-day Adventists to Clean on Last Sunday of the Month Instead of Saturday
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The Seventh-day Adventist Church has agreed with the Government of Uganda to conduct nationwide cleaning activities on the last Sunday of every month instead of Saturday, which is the official National Cleaning Day.
image_alt: Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja meeting SDA Church leaders
content: The Seventh-day Adventist (SDA) Church has reached consensus with the Government of Uganda on an alternative arrangement for the National Cleaning Day. Under the agreement, SDA members will conduct nationwide cleaning activities on every last Sunday of the month instead of Saturday. Led by Archbishop Samuel Kajoba, the SDA leaders also agreed to open worship centres at 10:00 a.m. every last Saturday of the month after the official national cleaning activities. The consensus was communicated on Tuesday evening during a meeting at the Office of the Prime Minister with Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja and the Deputy Secretary General of the NRM, Rt Hon Rose Namayanja. The National Cleaning Day is observed on the last Saturday of every month as part of government efforts to promote environmental cleanliness and community participation. The arrangement accommodates the SDA Church’s observance of Saturday as a day of worship while ensuring members contribute to the national sanitation exercise.

title: Museveni Swears In Three Ministers, Stresses Anti-Corruption and Loyalty
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Yoweri Museveni on Tuesday swore in three ministers at State House Entebbe: Ambassador Adonia Ayebare as Foreign Affairs Minister, Shartsi Kutesa Musherure as State Minister for Micro-Finance, and Juma Witonze as State Minister for Internal Affairs.
image_alt: President Museveni with newly sworn-in ministers at State House Entebbe
content: President Yoweri Museveni on Tuesday, 11 August 2026, presided over the swearing-in of three ministers at State House Entebbe. The new officials are Ambassador Adonia Ayebare as Minister of Foreign Affairs, Shartsi Kutesa Musherure as Minister of State for Finance, Planning and Economic Development in charge of Micro-Finance, and Juma Witonze Kisekka as Minister of State for Internal Affairs. In his remarks, Museveni congratulated the trio and directed them to prioritise the elimination of corruption and inefficiency through stronger supervision and accountability. He also addressed dual citizenship, stating that while the provision was introduced to address Uganda’s difficult history, individuals must be clear about where their loyalty lies. The President reiterated that the East African Federation remains the long-term solution to questions of identity and regional integration. Ambassador Ayebare, a seasoned diplomat and former Permanent Representative to the United Nations, replaces Gen Jeje Odongo at Foreign Affairs. His appointment signals a preference for professional diplomatic experience. Shartsi Kutesa Musherure, a lawyer and former Mawogola North MP, takes charge of the Micro-Finance docket that oversees programmes such as the Parish Development Model and Emyooga. Juma Witonze fills the Internal Affairs State Minister position after Parliament’s Appointments Committee rejected an earlier nominee over citizenship concerns. These appointments form part of the broader 2026–2031 Cabinet. Several nominees faced scrutiny over dual citizenship during parliamentary vetting, reflecting ongoing sensitivity around loyalty and constitutional eligibility for high office. The anti-corruption emphasis aligns with repeated presidential messaging since the start of the new term. Public expectations now centre on whether the new ministers will deliver clearer accountability and tangible results in their respective dockets.

title: President Directs Mariam Wangadya to Continue Serving as Human Rights Commission Boss
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Yoweri Museveni has rejected the resignation of Uganda Human Rights Commission Chairperson Mariam Fauzat Wangadya and instructed her to remain in office. Wangadya revealed this while appearing before Parliament’s COSASE committee.
image_alt: UHRC Chairperson Mariam Wangadya appearing before Parliament
content: President Yoweri Museveni has rejected the resignation of Uganda Human Rights Commission (UHRC) Chairperson Mariam Fauzat Wangadya and directed her to continue executing her mandate. Wangadya made the revelation on Tuesday while appearing before Parliament’s Committee on Commissions, Statutory Authorities and State Enterprises (COSASE). She said after submitting her resignation letter, the President declined to accept it and instructed her to keep serving. Wangadya formally tendered her resignation in a letter dated 6 July 2026. The move came days after she publicly criticised presidential appointments to the Commission, accusing the President of turning the UHRC into a “dumping ground for failed politicians.” Fellow commissioners later accused her of abandoning the institution and failing to convene meetings for several months. Wangadya countered that she had been subjected to a coordinated smear campaign. In an earlier parliamentary appearance she broke down in tears and apologised for her language. Attorney General Sam Mayanja had previously clarified that a resignation only takes effect once accepted by the appointing authority. Until then, Wangadya remained the substantive Chairperson. The President’s decision ends more than a month of uncertainty over the leadership of the constitutional body responsible for promoting and protecting human rights. The episode highlights ongoing tensions over the autonomy and composition of constitutional institutions. Wangadya now continues in office with a clear presidential directive. How she manages internal divisions and restores the Commission’s effectiveness will shape public confidence in one of Uganda’s key human rights watchdogs.

title: Committee Pauses Review of Auditor General’s Report as Two Officials Claim CEO Position at Insurance Regulatory Authority
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Parliament’s Committee on Commissions, Statutory Authorities and State Enterprises has paused scrutiny of the Auditor General’s report on the Insurance Regulatory Authority after two individuals appeared claiming the position of Chief Executive Officer.
image_alt: Parliament committee meeting on IRA leadership
content: Parliament’s Committee on Commissions, Statutory Authorities and State Enterprises has suspended scrutiny of the Auditor General’s report on the Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) following a leadership dispute. The pause came after Dr Protazio Sande appeared before the committee as Acting Chief Executive Officer, while Dr Ibrahim Kaddunabbi Lubega also presented himself as the Chief Executive Officer. Committee Chairperson Hon Muwada Nkunyingi (NUP, Kyadondo County East) said the committee will seek clarification from the Permanent Secretary and Secretary to the Treasury on who lawfully heads the Authority. Former Board Chairperson Dr Isaac Nkote Nabeta told the committee that the Board had declined to recommend Kaddunabbi for reappointment. Current Board Chairperson Keto Nyapendi Kayemba said that decision was upheld and Dr Sande was appointed in an acting capacity. The committee has also requested a copy of the court injunction in Kaddunabbi’s case. The High Court has halted the appointment of a substantive Chief Executive Officer while allowing Dr Sande to remain in the acting role pending determination of the dispute. The leadership row has temporarily halted parliamentary oversight of the Auditor General’s findings on the Authority.

title: First Daughter Thanks God as First Lady Reappears After Months Away from Public Eye
author: Musanya Musa
excerpt: Natasha Museveni Karugire has shared fresh photos with her mother, First Lady Janet Museveni, after months of limited public appearances due to illness. She captioned the post “Thank you, LORD Jesus!”
image_alt: Natasha Museveni Karugire with First Lady Janet Museveni
content: First daughter Natasha Museveni Karugire has shared touching new photos with her mother, First Lady Janet Museveni, marking a welcome return to the public eye. The images, posted on Monday, show the mother and daughter together in warm, relaxed moments. Natasha captioned the post simply: “Thank you, LORD Jesus!” The First Lady had been largely absent from public functions for several months following a serious illness. President Yoweri Museveni had earlier revealed that she fell critically ill in March but was recovering well, crediting doctors and divine intervention. The fresh photos have been widely shared across social media, with many Ugandans expressing joy at seeing the First Lady looking healthy and smiling alongside her daughter. The family moment comes as a relief to many who had followed the First Lady’s health updates with concern.

title: Susan Magara Sentencing Sparks Debate on Islamic Dress in Court and Collective Blame
author: Musanya Musa
excerpt: The High Court has sentenced nine people in the 2018 kidnap and murder of Susan Magara, with two receiving the death penalty. Public debate has shifted to the convicts’ Islamic attire in court and the risks of collective blame against the Muslim community.
image_alt: Convicts in the Susan Magara case during sentencing at the High Court
content: The High Court’s sentencing of nine people for the 2018 kidnap and murder of businesswoman Susan Magara has closed one of Uganda’s most notorious ransom-killing cases, yet it has opened a fresh wave of public debate. Hajara Nakandi and Abbas Musa Buwembo were sentenced to death. The remaining seven received life imprisonment. Justice Alex Mackay Ajiji described the crime as meticulously planned, extremely brutal and driven by financial gain. What has dominated social media discussion is not only the verdict but the appearance of several convicts in Islamic attire, including the kanzu, and with full beards. Critics have questioned why they were permitted to appear this way when prison regulations normally require hair to be trimmed, arguing that the presentation risked associating the crime with Islam. Court evidence showed a coordinated criminal group motivated by ransom. One convict, Ismail Bukenya, was an imam at a makeshift mosque in Usafi Market and was found to have hosted planning meetings. The case was prosecuted as organised criminality, not as a religiously mandated act. Senior Muslim clerics have strongly rejected any attempt to link the murder to Islamic teaching. Deputy Mufti Sheikh Muhammad Ali Waiswa and Uganda Muslim Supreme Council National Chairperson Prof Muhammadi Lubega Kisambira described such claims as false and dangerous. They acknowledged that individuals from every community commit crimes but insisted that associating this atrocity with the faith itself is inaccurate and harmful.
