Prison regulations generally require standardised appearance. Allowing full beards and Islamic dress for the court appearance has raised legitimate questions about consistency. Whether this was routine religious accommodation, a choice by the defence, or something more deliberate remains a matter of interpretation. It is true that several high-profile violent cases in recent years have involved Muslim suspects. This has created a recurring public narrative. At the same time, Uganda’s Muslim population is large, diverse and overwhelmingly law-abiding. Collective guilt is both factually weak and socially dangerous. It fuels prejudice and can be exploited for other ends. The correct response remains individual accountability under the law and equal application of rules, including prison dress and grooming standards, regardless of religion. A brutal murder case should produce clarity about guilt and punishment. Instead, the accompanying debate risks becoming another arena for communal polarisation. Justice has been delivered against specific people for specific acts. That is where accountability must remain. King Musah Media will continue following the implementation of the sentences and related public discourse.

title: CEO Musanya Musa Reflects on Journey from COVID-19 Idea to Technology, Media and Education Brands
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: KMVTECHUG is marking its sixth anniversary. What began as a YouTube channel during the COVID-19 pandemic has grown into an ecosystem of media, technology and education brands under the leadership of CEO Musanya Musa.
image_alt: KMVTECHUG sixth anniversary celebration
content: Six years ago, during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, Musanya Musa started a YouTube channel called King Musah Media with a simple slogan: “Driving Your Imagination to Reality.” What began as a platform for entertainment news and trending stories has today evolved into KMVTECHUG — an umbrella organisation that brings together media, technology solutions and education under one vision. In a statement marking the anniversary, CEO Musanya Musa traced the journey from those early uploads to the current ecosystem. One video listing some of Uganda’s most beautiful artists crossed 16,000 views within two months, giving the young creator the first real signal that the idea had potential. When passion alone could not cover data, transport and equipment costs, King Musah Visuals was born with the slogan “Scripting a New World.” Graphic design work soon expanded into broader IT needs websites, software and technical support, leading to the creation of KMVTECH and eventually the umbrella brand KMVTECHUG. Today the organisation comprises three main pillars. King Musah Media has grown beyond entertainment into a broader news and information platform. KMVTECH provides technology and digital solutions, including websites and systems. KMVTECH EDUCATION, launched on 8 August 2025, focuses on making learning materials and opportunities more accessible to students. A major milestone this year has been the launch of the company’s permanent digital home at kmvtechug.app. The platform is being developed into a learning environment where students will access online courses and eventually earn certifications. Testing, originally planned for 8 August, has been deliberately delayed to ensure quality. Musa acknowledged that the six years have not been without struggle. Systems went down, computers remained unrepaired for months due to limited resources, clients sometimes failed to pay, and the team often relied on temporary staff. An earlier attempt to expand King Musah Media into KMMTv Online was put on hold after it failed to take off as planned. “Building a company is not only about having good ideas. It is about surviving long enough, learning enough and becoming disciplined enough to turn those ideas into sustainable institutions,” Musa said. He paid tribute to the team that works behind the scenes, clients who trusted the young brand, partners and everyone who supported the vision when there was little to show. Looking ahead, KMVTECHUG is completing formal company registration, strengthening its permanent team, building more sophisticated systems and preparing for deeper partnerships. Musa described the start of the seventh year as a transition — from individual projects to institution-building, from survival to sustainable structures. “Six years ago, we were driving your imagination to reality. Today, we are scripting a new world. And tomorrow, we intend to build one that is better than what we have today,” he stated. King Musah Media congratulates the entire KMVTECHUG team on this milestone.

title: Ruhamya Kainerugaba Graduates from Sandhurst as Father Looks On
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Officer Cadet Ruhamya Kainerugaba, son of Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba and grandson of President Museveni, has graduated from the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst. Fellow Ugandan Andrew Bakira Ruyondo was awarded the International Sword.
image_alt: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba with his son Ruhamya at Sandhurst graduation
content: Officer Cadet Ruhamya Kainerugaba has completed the 44-week Officer Commissioning Course at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst in the United Kingdom. His father, Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, attended the Sovereign’s Parade. The Academy Commandant received the CDF and later presented him with a Sandhurst Alumni medal. Gen Muhoozi had earlier posted side-by-side images comparing his own Sandhurst experience in the class of 2000 with his son’s, noting “father and son going through the same hardships, separated by 27 years.” Fellow Ugandan cadet Andrew Bakira Ruyondo graduated in the same intake and was awarded the International Sword, given to the outstanding international cadet. State Minister Lillian Aber congratulated Ruhamya, describing the moment as “a proud moment for Gen Muhoozi & family, the Uganda People’s Defence Forces, and the entire nation.” Sandhurst remains one of the world’s most prestigious military academies. Completing the course is a rigorous personal achievement. Uganda regularly sends selected officers there. Yet in the current political climate the graduation carries wider meaning. Gen Muhoozi is not only the CDF but a highly visible political figure who has openly expressed presidential ambitions and built the Patriotic League of Uganda. The father-son Sandhurst pathway reinforces perceptions of multi-generational military-political continuity in a country where the armed forces remain central to power. While Bakira Ruyondo’s award demonstrates that other Ugandans can excel on pure performance, the heavy official focus on Ruhamya has prompted public discussion about selection, privilege and institutional culture. The real test for the next generation of officers — including those with family ties to power — will be whether they prioritise the Constitution, the rule of law and the rights of citizens over personal or dynastic loyalty. For now, the images of father and son at Sandhurst stand as both a personal milestone and a public signal. How Ugandans read that signal depends on their assessment of the country’s democratic health and the role of the military within it. King Musah Media will continue following developments in the defence and political spheres.

title: Youth Parliament Adopts Key Motions on Sexual and Reproductive Health, Climate Action and Road Safety
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Following the reproductive health motion, the House adopted a resolution on climate action, environmental protection and the building of climate-resilient communities. Youth delegates highlighted the disproportionate impact of climate change on young people and called for stronger government interventions in environmental protection and community resilience.
image_alt: Youth parliament
content: The Second Sitting of the 8th Uganda National Youth Parliament, held at Parliament on 7 August 2026, saw youth delegates debate and adopt a series of progressive motions aimed at addressing critical challenges facing young people. Under the theme “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations,” the sitting, chaired by Youth Parliament Speaker Rodney Adroni, focused on sexual and reproductive health, climate resilience, road safety, national security, youth employment and meaningful participation in governance.

The event was opened by Deputy Speaker of Parliament Rt. Hon. Thomas Tayebwa and attended by Minister of State for Youth and Children Affairs Dr. Lakisa Mercy Faith, among other dignitaries. Resolutions from the Youth Parliament are expected to be formally received by Parliament for consideration by relevant committees and government institutions.
Motion on Sexual and Reproductive Health Adopted

A central highlight of the sitting was the successful adoption of a motion urging Government to enhance access to accurate sexual and reproductive health information for adolescents and young people. Moved and debated under Speaker Adroni, the motion received broad support from youth delegates before being put to the question and passed

Delegates emphasised the importance of knowledge as a tool for protection, enabling young people to understand their bodies, recognise health changes, prevent unintended pregnancies and reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections. Speakers stressed that access to factual information does not promote early sexual activity but empowers responsible decision-making and reduces vulnerability to myths, peer pressure and misinformation.

The discussion also touched on menstrual health equity, with calls for greater availability of free menstrual products in public facilities, drawing parallels with existing free condom distribution programmes. The motion aligns with ongoing national efforts, including programmes under the Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development aimed at preventing teenage pregnancy and expanding life skills education.
Climate Action and Road Safety Motions Advanced

Following the reproductive health motion, the House adopted a resolution on climate action, environmental protection and the building of climate-resilient communities. Youth delegates highlighted the disproportionate impact of climate change on young people and called for stronger government interventions in environmental protection and community resilience.

The sitting then moved to a motion on road safety, crime prevention, access to justice, service delivery and national security, moved by Emmanuel Edonu and seconded by Deo Mutuma. Debates underscored the high rate of road traffic deaths involving young people, particularly motorcycle riders, and stressed the dual need for government action and personal responsibility. Speakers called for improved road safety education, better enforcement of traffic rules, expanded access to mediation and alternative justice mechanisms for young people who cannot afford formal legal representation.

Earlier in the sitting, a motion on enhancing youth employment through skills development and enterprise growth was also adopted, reflecting persistent concerns about job creation and economic empowerment for Uganda’s youthful population.
Political Analysis: Youth Voices Shaping the National Agenda

As a senior journalist and political analyst, this sitting of the National Youth Parliament represents a significant platform for intergenerational dialogue and policy influence. Unlike purely symbolic exercises, previous Youth Parliament resolutions have informed parliamentary discussions and legislative considerations, demonstrating the growing institutional recognition of organised youth advocacy.

The focus on sexual and reproductive health is particularly timely. With high rates of teenage pregnancy remaining a national challenge, accurate information, accessible services and stigma-free environments are essential for protecting the health, education and future productivity of young Ugandans. Equally important are the climate and road safety motions, which address existential risks that disproportionately affect the youth demographic.

Speaker Rodney Adroni’s insistence on evidence-based submissions, decorum and time consciousness set a professional tone that elevated the quality of debate. The presence of senior government and parliamentary leaders further signalled that youth recommendations are being taken seriously.

The true test, however, will lie in follow-through. As Deputy Speaker Tayebwa proposed, future sittings should include action-taken reports so that young people can track the progress of their resolutions. Only then will the Youth Parliament move from being a valuable deliberative space to a sustained engine of accountability and policy change.
King Musah Media will continue to follow the transmission of these resolutions to Parliament and the response of relevant government ministries and agencies.

title: Health Minister Baryomunsi Visits Besigye at Mulago, Says He Is Steadily Recovering
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Health Minister Dr Chris Baryomunsi has visited Dr Kizza Besigye at Mulago National Referral Hospital and reported that the veteran opposition leader is steadily recovering. Besigye has been in detention for nearly two years.
image_alt: Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi
content: Health Minister Dr Chris Baryomunsi on Friday visited detained opposition leader Dr Kizza Besigye at Mulago National Referral Hospital and said he is steadily recuperating. “I paid a visit to Dr Kiiza Besigye today morning at Mulago Hospital, where he is hospitalised. He is steadily recuperating and I wished him quick recovery. I thank the team of medical workers that are attending to him,” Baryomunsi stated. Besigye has been in detention for nearly two years and is currently facing a treason-related trial at the High Court together with Hajj Obeid Lutale and Capt Denis Oola. He was admitted to Mulago after collapsing in the dock during court proceedings on 29 July. The minister’s visit comes as debate continues over Besigye’s health, access to his preferred medical care, and the conditions of his prolonged detention. Family members and supporters have previously called for independent medical attention and raised concerns about his treatment while in custody. Court proceedings in the treason case have faced repeated delays linked to Besigye’s health status.

title: Two Next Media Journalists Killed in Entebbe Road Crash, Colleague in ICU
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Two employees of Next Media Services, Badru Kasirye and Isaac Ndamagye, have died in a road accident along Entebbe Road early Friday morning. Their colleague Brian “Makona” Ssemanda is in intensive care
image_alt: Scene of the fatal accident at Namulanda on Entebbe Road
content: Two journalists working with Next Media Services have died in a fatal road crash along Entebbe Road, while a third remains in critical condition. Badru Kasirye and Isaac Ndamagye died at the scene in the early hours of Friday, 7 August 2026. Their colleague, entertainment journalist Brian Ssemanda, popularly known as Makona, sustained serious injuries and was rushed to Kisubi Hospital, where he is receiving treatment in the Intensive Care Unit. According to Uganda Police, the accident occurred at about 2:00 a.m. at Namulanda near the Stabex fuel station. It involved a Toyota Allex registration UA 779DE carrying the three Next Media staff and a Toyota Hilux registration UAS 976W. Preliminary investigations indicate that the driver of the Hilux, which was travelling from Entebbe towards Kampala, lost control and drifted into the opposite lane, resulting in a head-on collision. Next Media Services confirmed the deaths and asked for privacy for the families of the deceased and for Makona as he continues treatment. The three had reportedly been returning from covering a celebrity boxing event. Police have extended condolences to the families and colleagues of the deceased and wished Makona a quick recovery. Investigations into the exact cause of the crash are ongoing. King Musah Media joins the media fraternity in mourning the loss of Badru Kasirye and Isaac Ndamagye and prays for the full recovery of Brian Makona.

title: Ogwang Assures Parliament that Aki-Bua Stadium and Other Venues Will Meet CAF Standards
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Sports Minister Peter Ogwang has told Parliament that government is on course to deliver three stadiums to host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. CAF has agreed that Aki-Bua Stadium can host matches if required standards are met.
image_alt: Sports Minister Peter Ogwang speaking in Parliament
content: Sports Minister Peter Ogwang has assured Parliament that government is on course to deliver three stadiums to host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON). Speaking during plenary, Ogwang said he wrote to the Confederation of African Football (CAF) requesting an inspection of Aki-Bua Stadium. CAF agreed that the facility can host AFCON matches if government commits to delivering the required standards. “The contractor is working at 120 percent to beat the December deadline,” the Minister told MPs. Uganda is co-hosting AFCON 2027 with other East African nations. The successful delivery of modern, CAF-compliant stadiums remains a key requirement for the tournament. Ogwang’s statement comes amid ongoing public interest in the readiness of sports infrastructure ahead of the continental showpiece. King Musah Media will continue tracking progress on AFCON 2027 preparations. Teaser:
Sports Minister Peter Ogwang has told Parliament that government is on course to deliver three stadiums for AFCON 2027, with Aki-Bua Stadium cleared by CAF subject to meeting required standards.

title: Museveni in Tanzania at Invitation of President Samia Suluhu Hassan to Strengthen Bilateral Ties
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Yoweri Museveni has arrived in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, for a two-day official visit at the invitation of President Samia Suluhu Hassan. The visit aims to strengthen Uganda-Tanzania relations.
image_alt: President Museveni arriving in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
content: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni has arrived in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, for a two-day official visit. The visit is at the invitation of Tanzanian President Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan. According to Minister of State for Internal Affairs Juma Witonze Kisekka, the engagements will focus on strengthening Uganda-Tanzania relations through enhanced cooperation in trade, infrastructure, energy, security, tourism and regional integration. The two East African neighbours share longstanding historical, economic and political ties. Discussions are expected to advance mutual interests within the framework of the East African Community and broader regional stability. King Musah Media will continue monitoring outcomes of the presidential visit.

title: Kiryowa Kiwanuka Seeks Parliamentary Support for UPDF Priorities and Ongoing Programmes
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Defence Minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka appeared before the Parliamentary Committee on Defence and Internal Affairs to present the state of the Ministry of Defence and Veterans Affairs, key achievements and resource requirements for the UPDF.
image_alt: Defence Minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka appearing before the Parliamentary Committee on Defence and Internal Affairs
content: The Minister of Defence and Veterans Affairs, Kiryowa Kiwanuka, on Tuesday appeared before the Parliamentary Committee on Defence and Internal Affairs to present the state of the ministry, accountability and resource needs of the Ministry of Defence and Veterans Affairs (MODVA) and the UPDF. He was accompanied by the Minister of State for Defence, Grace Akifeza Ngabirano, and the Minister of State for Veteran Affairs, Huda Abason Oleru. The committee is chaired by Robina Rwakoojo. Kiwanuka briefed MPs on the constitutional mandate of the UPDF under Article 208 and outlined key achievements recorded between 2021 and 2026. These include sustained peace and security during elections, acquisition and maintenance of strategic equipment, consistent annual recruitment of about 10,000 personnel, and continuous professional training. He noted the establishment of the National Defence College–Uganda in 2022, which has so far graduated 83 students. On welfare, the minister reported phased salary and pension enhancements, full and timely pension payments totalling more than Shs 540 billion, and progress on a 250-bed UPDF National Referral Hospital. Infrastructure gains include the construction of 30,000 housing units for the force (1,000 completed so far) and ongoing work on the MODVA/UPDF headquarters, expected to be commissioned by 30 September 2026. Kiwanuka tabled several requests for parliamentary support, including backing for peace support operations, legislation for an autonomous UPDF National Referral Hospital, and duty-free status for the Defence Forces Shop. He also cited challenges such as inadequate budget, delayed AUSSOM funds and housing shortages. The ministers reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to a professional, disciplined and productive force subordinate to civilian authority.

title: Two Sentenced to Death, Seven Get Life in Susan Magara Murder Case
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The High Court has sentenced Hajara Nakandi and Abbas Musa Buwembo to death for their central roles in the 2018 kidnap and murder of Susan Magara. The remaining seven convicts received life imprisonment.
image_alt: The nine convicts in the Susan Magara case during sentencing at the High Court
content: The High Court in Kampala has sentenced two of the nine people convicted over the kidnap and murder of Susan Magara to death, while the other seven will serve life imprisonment. Justice Alex Mackay Ajiji on Wednesday sentenced Hajara Nakandi and Abbas Musa Buwembo (also referred to as Buvumbo) to suffer death. The court found they played the most direct roles in the killing. Nakandi was found to have remained with Magara throughout her captivity and influenced the decision to kill her after the victim had spent enough time with the group to identify them. Buwembo carried out the most violent acts, including severing two of Magara’s fingers during ransom negotiations, injecting her with ketamine and suffocating her. The seven others — Yusuf Lubega, Mahad Kisalita, Ismail Bukenya, Abubaker Kyewokya, Hassan Wasswa, Hussein Kato Miiro and Muzamir Ssali — were sentenced to life imprisonment for their roles in planning, aiding and facilitating the offences. Justice Ajiji ruled that the aggravating factors, including the premeditated and highly organised nature of the crime, the extreme brutality and the financial motive, far outweighed any mitigating circumstances. He also appreciated the investigators who worked on the case. The court ordered the confiscation and forfeiture of properties acquired using the ransom money, including land in Buikwe and Luweero as well as vehicles, with proceeds to be paid to Magara’s family. Magara, 28, was abducted in February 2018, held for nearly three weeks and murdered despite her family paying a substantial ransom. The convicts have 14 days to appeal.

title: Musasizi and Lugoloobi Urge Enterprise Uganda to Leverage Technology for Wider Entrepreneurship Support
author: Musanya Musa
excerpt: Finance Minister Henry Musasizi and State Minister for Planning Amos Lugoloobi have challenged Enterprise Uganda to use digital platforms to reach more Ugandans with entrepreneurship and business support services.
image_alt: Finance Minister Henry Musasizi and State Minister Amos Lugoloobi meeting the Enterprise Uganda Board
content: The Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, Henry Musasizi, together with the Minister of State for Planning, Amos Lugoloobi, have challenged Enterprise Uganda to leverage digital platforms to expand its reach. The call was made during a meeting with the Board of Management of Enterprise Uganda, led by Board Chairperson Richard Byarugaba and Executive Director Charles Ocici. The discussions focused on the institution’s contribution to entrepreneurship development and its role in advancing Uganda’s private sector-led growth agenda. Enterprise Uganda, established 25 years ago with support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), is the country’s leading provider of entrepreneurship development and Business Development Services. Musasizi commended the organisation for its contribution to private sector development and recognised the Board’s commitment to strong corporate governance. He emphasised the need to deepen post-training mentorship and provide continuous business support that enables entrepreneurs to build sustainable enterprises. Lugoloobi called for stronger monitoring, evaluation and transparent reporting to demonstrate impact and attract greater public and private investment. He also recommended integrating entrepreneurship education into secondary schools, universities and tertiary institutions, and proposed orientation programmes for newly elected Members of Parliament on financial management, investment and wealth creation. The ministers reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to supporting Enterprise Uganda as a strategic partner in promoting entrepreneurship, enterprise growth and inclusive economic transformation.

title: Malende Raises Kampala Garbage Crisis in Parliament as Government Pledges Action
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Kampala Woman MP Shamim Malende has raised the continued accumulation of uncollected garbage in parts of the city as a matter of national importance. Government responded that KCCA is scaling up efforts and will provide additional trucks.
image_alt: ampala Woman MP Shamim Malende speaking in Parliament
content: Kampala Woman MP Shamim Malende has asked Government to explain the persistent heaps of uncollected garbage across parts of the capital following the recent National Cleaning Day. Raising the issue as a matter of national importance in Parliament on Tuesday, Malende said communities in Lubaga, Kawempe, Makindye and Central Division are grappling with uncollected waste. She warned that the situation poses a serious public health risk. The MP called on the line minister to outline immediate measures being taken to clear the garbage and long-term plans to ensure timely waste disposal after future National Cleaning Day exercises. Responding on behalf of Government, Chief Whip Dr Jane Ruth Aceng said Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA) has intensified efforts to improve waste collection across the city. Aceng told Parliament that KCCA has doubled its efforts to ensure timely garbage disposal and that additional garbage trucks will be provided to strengthen waste management going forward. The exchange highlights ongoing challenges with solid waste management in Kampala despite periodic city-wide cleaning campaigns.

title: Besigye Unable to Appear in Court as Prisons Officer Confirms He Remains at Mulago
author: Musanya Musa
excerpt: A prisons officer has informed the High Court that Dr Kizza Besigye remains admitted at Mulago Hospital and cannot appear for his treason trial. The defence has asked that a medical doctor present the health report instead.
image_alt: Besigye Unable to Appear in Court as Prisons Officer Confirms He Remains at Mulago
content: A prisons officer has told the High Court that veteran opposition politician Dr Kizza Besigye is still admitted at Mulago National Referral Hospital and is unable to appear for his ongoing treason trial. The update was given on Tuesday during proceedings before Justice Emmanuel Baguma. Besigye is jointly charged with Hajj Obeid Lutale and Capt Denis Oola. Defence lawyers argued that Besigye’s continued absence affects his right to a fair trial. They requested that a medical doctor, rather than a prisons officer, be allowed to present his health report to the court. Prosecution counsel responded that they had not yet reviewed the medical letter. They further submitted that an accused person’s constitutional right to be present during trial is not absolute. Besigye collapsed in the dock on 29 July during an earlier hearing and was rushed to Mulago, where he has remained under treatment. The trial has faced repeated delays linked to his health and questions over legal representation. Court is expected to determine the way forward after considering the medical information and submissions from both sides.

title: Pepsi Uganda Welcomes Ghetto Kids Home After World Cup Final Performance
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Pepsi Uganda has officially welcomed home the Ghetto Kids following their historic performance at the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final halftime show. The young dancers shared the stage with global stars Shakira and Burna Boy.
image_alt: Ghetto Kids being welcomed home by Pepsi Uganda
content: Pepsi Uganda has rolled out a warm homecoming for the Ghetto Kids after their groundbreaking appearance at the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final. The Kampala-based dance troupe performed during the first-ever official World Cup Final halftime show at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on 19 July. They joined Colombian superstar Shakira and Nigerian artist Burna Boy on the tournament anthem “Dai Dai,” captivating a global audience. The group, also known as Triplets Ghetto Kids, returned to Uganda on Monday to jubilant receptions at Entebbe International Airport and subsequent celebrations. Fans, family and supporters turned out in numbers, waving flags and cheering the young performers who have become cultural ambassadors for the country. Pepsi Uganda, which has long supported the troupe, formally welcomed them back as history-makers. The Uganda Tourism Board also joined in celebrating their achievement, noting that the performance introduced millions worldwide to the creativity and spirit of Uganda. Founded to support disadvantaged children through music, dance and drama, the Ghetto Kids first gained international attention through viral dance videos. Their World Cup appearance marks the highest global platform they have reached so far. King Musah Media congratulates the Ghetto Kids on making Uganda proud.

title: URSB Deregisters 90,000 Inactive Companies in Massive Compliance Crackdown
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The Uganda Registration Services Bureau has officially deregistered 90,000 companies that failed to file annual returns for five consecutive years and did not apply for restoration within the given grace period. The action was taken under the Companies Act.
image_alt: URSB head offices in Kampala
content: The Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB) has deregistered 90,000 inactive companies in one of its largest compliance clean-ups in recent years.  In a notice issued on 3 August 2026, the Registrar of Companies confirmed that the entities were removed pursuant to Section 130(6) of the Companies Act, Cap. 106. The companies had failed to file annual returns for five consecutive years and did not utilise the 12-month administrative restoration window that followed public notices issued in 2023.  URSB Principal Communication Officer Dennis Nabende said the move is aimed at maintaining a clean, credible and functional business register.  “Annual returns are not just paperwork. They tell us and the public whether a company is still active and whether its details are current,” Nabende stated. “When companies fail to file for five years, the law requires us to strike them off.”  Deregistered companies immediately lose legal personality. They can no longer enter contracts, open bank accounts, sue or be sued in their registered names. Their names also return to the public domain and can be taken by any third party.  The full list of the 90,000 companies has been published on the URSB official portal. Former owners who still hold assets or pending contracts under the deregistered entities must now apply to the High Court for reinstatement.  URSB has urged all active companies to file their annual returns promptly and keep their records updated to avoid a similar fate.  King Musah Media will continue following corporate compliance developments.

title: UPDF Pulls Out of NMG Offices After Weeks of Occupation as Management Conducts Safety Checks
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The Uganda People’s Defence Forces have finally withdrawn from the premises of Nation Media Group Uganda. Management has, however, advised staff not to return immediately as the company’s internal security team continues safety and security assessments.
image_alt: Nation Media Group offices in Namuwongo
content: The army has finally withdrawn from the premises of Nation Media Group Uganda after weeks of occupation.  According to a report by The Observer, management has cautioned staff against returning to the offices immediately. The company’s internal security team is still conducting thorough safety and security assessments before the premises can be fully reopened.  “A lot of checks are ongoing, and we shouldn’t compromise that exercise,” the internal communication stated.  The military presence at NMG facilities in Namuwongo and the Kampala Serena International Conference Centre began in the early hours of 28 June 2026. Soldiers sealed off the premises following public directives by Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, forcing NTV Uganda, Spark TV, Daily Monitor, KFM and Dembe FM off air and out of print.  The government later described the action as part of a security-led inquiry instituted by President Museveni. Operations began a phased resumption in late July after clearance, but soldiers remained on site until this week.  The full withdrawal marks a significant step toward normalising activities at one of Uganda’s largest media houses.  King Musah Media will continue monitoring the situation as NMG completes its internal assessments.

title: 14 Killed in Fatal Crash Between Taxi and Sand Truck in Lwera Swamp
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Fourteen people died on the spot in a fatal road accident in Lwera Swamp, Kalungu District, on the night of 3 August 2026. A Toyota Hiace taxi collided with a Sino truck carrying sand along the Kampala–Masaka Highway.
image_alt: Scene of the fatal accident in Lwera Swamp, Kalungu District
content: Fourteen people have died in a fatal road crash in Lwera Swamp, Kamunga Trading Centre, along the Kampala–Masaka Highway.  According to Uganda Police, the accident occurred around 11:00 pm on 3 August 2026. It involved a Toyota Hiace taxi registration UA 662AQ and a Sino truck registration UBS 040F that was transporting sand.  All 14 victims who died on the spot were travelling in the taxi. Four other people — two from each vehicle — sustained injuries and were admitted to Masaka Regional Referral Hospital.  Police visited the scene and have launched investigations. Efforts are underway to trace the driver of one of the vehicles who fled after the collision.  Lwera Swamp on the Kampala–Masaka road has been the site of several serious accidents in the past, often linked to poor visibility, speeding and the nature of the terrain.

title: Works Minister Directs Contractor to Speed Up Kira–Kasangati–Matugga Road
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Works and Transport Minister Fred Byamukama has directed the contractor on the Kira–Kasangati–Matugga Road to immediately accelerate works following the resolution of key land issues. Clear deadlines have been set for critical sections of the project.
image_alt: Works Minister Fred Byamukama inspecting the Kira–Kasangati–Matugga Road
content: Works and Transport Minister Fred Byamukama has ordered the contractor handling the Kira–Kasangati–Matugga Road to speed up construction after government resolved outstanding land challenges. During an inspection focused on results rather than routine checks, the Minister emphasised that every delayed road project costs citizens time, business and opportunities. He directed that the Kyaliwajjala–Kira–Kasangati section must reach the junction by December 2026. The remaining stretch to Matugga is required to be completed by July 2027. Byamukama also instructed the contractor to maintain regular dust control and upkeep on all sections currently under construction. Government will complete payments to the remaining project-affected persons to remove the last barriers to progress. The Minister’s intervention comes amid public concern over the pace of several road projects in the greater Kampala area. King Musah Media will continue monitoring progress on the Kira–Kasangati–Matugga corridor.

title: Nambeshe Welcomes Nine NUP Supporters Freed After More Than Six Years in Detention
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: NUP Acting President and Manjiya MP John Baptist Nambeshe on Monday officially welcomed nine party supporters who regained their freedom after more than six years in detention. The group was released last week through the Amnesty Commission process.
image_alt: John Baptist Nambeshe with the nine released NUP supporters at a press conference
content: National Unity Platform Acting President John Baptist Nambeshe on Monday addressed a press conference to formally welcome nine party supporters freed after spending more than six years in detention. Nambeshe described their resilience in the face of what the party terms political persecution as truly inspiring. The nine had been held largely without a concluded fair trial in a civilian court. Those released include Yasin Ssekitoleko (alias Yasin Machete), Patrick Mwase, Sharif Kalanzi, Joseph Muwonge, Abdallah Kintu, Umar Emma Kato, Musa Kavuma, Jimmy Galukande and Abdallah Gibusiwa. They were among supporters arrested around the 2020–2021 election period and charged before the General Court Martial with treachery and unlawful possession of ammunition, among other allegations linked to a purported rebel group. After prolonged remand, the group applied for and was granted amnesty. The military court referred them to the Amnesty Commission, which issued certificates leading to their release at the end of July. NUP has consistently maintained that the charges were politically motivated and that the long detention without timely trial amounted to an abuse of the justice system. The party leadership used the occasion to reiterate calls for the release of remaining political prisoners. King Musah Media will continue following developments on political detentions and reintegration of those released.

title: High Court Convicts All Nine Accused in Susan Magara Kidnap and Murder Case
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The High Court in Kampala has convicted all nine accused persons in the 2018 kidnap and murder of businesswoman Susan Magara. Justice Alex Mackay Ajiji ruled that the prosecution proved the charges of kidnap with intent to procure a ransom and murder beyond reasonable doubt. Sentencing is scheduled for Tuesday.
image_alt: The nine accused in the Susan Magara case in the dock at High Court
content: The High Court Criminal Division in Kampala has convicted all nine people charged in the kidnap and murder of Susan Magara. On Monday, Justice Alex Mackay Ajiji delivered an 84-page judgment finding Yusuf Lubega, Mahad Kisalita, Ismail Bukenya, Abubaker Kyewokya, Hassan Wasswa, Abbas Musa Buwembo, Hussein Kato Miiro, Hajjara Nakandi and Muzamir Ssali guilty of kidnapping Magara with intent to obtain a ransom and the consequential murder. The Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions described the outcome as justice served. The judge agreed with the court assessors that the prosecution had proved its case against each of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. Magara, 28, was abducted on 7 February 2018 while driving home in Lungujja, Kampala. Her vehicle was found abandoned with the engine still running. She was held captive for nearly three weeks as the kidnappers demanded a large ransom. Despite the family paying about $200,000, she was killed. Her body was later recovered along the Entebbe Expressway. The nine maintained their innocence throughout the long trial. The matter has been adjourned to Tuesday for allocutus (mitigation) and sentencing. A murder conviction in Uganda carries a maximum penalty of death. The case, one of the most high-profile ransom killings in recent years, has lasted eight years from investigation to conviction. King Musah Media will follow the sentencing proceedings.

title: Museveni Presents Olara Otunnu as Uganda’s Candidate for UN Secretary-General
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Yoweri Museveni on Monday formally presented Ambassador Olara Otunnu as Uganda’s candidate for the position of United Nations Secretary-General. He urged ambassadors of UN Security Council member states to convey Uganda’s endorsement to their governments.
image_alt: President Museveni meeting ambassadors of UN Security Council member states at State House Entebbe
content: President Yoweri Museveni has formally presented Ambassador Olara Otunnu as Uganda’s candidate for United Nations Secretary-General. The presentation took place on Monday at State House Entebbe during a meeting with ambassadors representing members of the United Nations Security Council. Museveni urged the envoys to convey Uganda’s full endorsement of Otunnu to their respective governments. He described the veteran diplomat as a candidate with the experience, integrity and diplomatic credentials required to lead the world body. The President highlighted Uganda’s record in promoting regional peace and security, as well as its long-standing role as a host of refugees, as values that underpin the country’s support for Otunnu’s candidature. Otunnu, a former UN Under-Secretary-General and the first Special Representative for Children and Armed Conflict (1998–2005), previously served as Uganda’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations (1980–1985) and as President of the Security Council in December 1981. He also held the post of Minister of Foreign Affairs. His nomination places him among the candidates seeking to succeed the current UN Secretary-General when the term ends later this year.

title: President Museveni Hits Back at Andrew Mwenda Over Stephen Nuwagaba, Insists Torture Has No Place in the Struggle
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Yoweri Museveni has strongly rejected journalist Andrew Mwenda’s claims that Stephen Nuwagaba has laid “siege” on State House and security agencies. In a detailed statement, the President describes Nuwagaba as a torture victim he rescued and reaffirms that torture remains immoral and counter-revolutionary.
image_alt: President Yoweri Museveni
content: President Yoweri Museveni has issued a lengthy response to veteran journalist Andrew Mwenda over claims that a young man named Stephen Nuwagaba has seized control of State House and security institutions. In an article published in The Independent, Mwenda accused Nuwagaba, a man in his mid-twenties, of blackmailing public officials by threatening to report them to the President, extorting money and spreading false intelligence while claiming proximity to State House. Museveni dismissed the narrative as another of Mwenda’s “schemes.” He said Nuwagaba came to him as a fugitive and victim of torture and maiming by some elements within the security services who were also threatening to kill him. “He has actually been a patient on account of torture and maiming and trauma… for many of the months he has been under my care,” the President wrote. He stated that he arranged treatment for Nuwagaba both in Uganda and abroad. Some of the alleged perpetrators are now facing court charges. Museveni insisted that torture and maiming are “immoral, counter-revolutionary, not strategic and not necessary.” He declared that in 56 years of struggle he has never tortured or ordered the torture of an opponent. He accused Mwenda of focusing on “trivialities” and possibly covering up crimes instead of investigating larger problems such as corruption in the Parish Development Model (PDM) and road projects. The President said a quiet investigation into the matter is already underway. The statement comes amid ongoing public debate over security excesses and accountability. King Musah Media will continue following the exchanges and any official investigations.

title: Bayigga and Spire Challenge President Museveni Over Condition of Missing Activist Sam Mugumya
author: Musanya Musa
excerpt: Buikwe South MP Dr Bayigga Lulume and philosopher-cartoonist Jim Spire Ssentongo have publicly challenged President Yoweri Museveni over the leaked video of long-missing opposition activist Sam Mugumya. Both posts question the continued silence and suffering amid official denials of his detention.
image_alt: Still from the leaked video of Sam Mugumya using a walking frame
content: Buikwe South MP and physician Dr Bayigga Lulume has addressed an open letter to President Yoweri Museveni following the circulation of a leaked video showing opposition activist Sam Mugumya in a frail state. In the post accompanying the footage, Bayigga described the person who recorded and shared the video as a “courageous son of Uganda.” He reminded the President of his positions as Commander-in-Chief, appointing authority and a leader who often references the Bible and is addressed as “Jajja.” Bayigga asked how much more suffering Museveni would like to see and how many more such videos would need to reach him before action is taken. Philosopher, teacher and cartoonist Jim Spire Ssentongo shared a separate clip of the President speaking, captioning it: “If he meant it, maybe he’s no longer in charge.” The post has been widely interpreted as a reference to past government assurances against torture and incommunicado detention. The interventions come days after National Unity Platform leader Robert Kyagulanyi (Bobi Wine) first shared the video, which shows Mugumya struggling to walk with the aid of a walking frame. Mugumya has been missing since his reported abduction from a Mbarara hotel on 26 August 2025. Security agencies have consistently denied holding him. The authenticity of the video has not been independently verified by mainstream media or official investigators. No formal response from State House or security agencies to the latest appeals had been issued by Monday morning. Family, supporters and human rights voices continue to demand that Mugumya be produced before court and granted medical care if in custody. King Musah Media will keep following the matter.

title: Dr Moses Mukose Freed on Bond After Overnight Detention for Being Near Kizza Besigye’s Hospital Room
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Dr Moses Mukose has been released on police bond after spending more than 20 hours in custody. He was arrested at Mulago National Referral Hospital for allegedly wandering on the VIP floor where Dr Kizza Besigye is admitted under tight security.
image_alt: Dr Moses Mukose
content: Dr Moses Mukose, a former Inspectorate of Government commissioner and People’s Front for Freedom (PFF) Busoga Governor, has been released on police bond after overnight detention. Police arrested him on Saturday, 1 August 2026, at Mulago National Referral Hospital. Officers accused him of “wandering” or disobeying lawful orders on the sixth floor of the VIP wing — the same floor where opposition leader Dr Kizza Besigye is receiving treatment under heavy security. Mukose’s son, Arnold Anthony Mukose, said his father had gone to the hospital to visit his father-in-law, who has been admitted to the Intensive Care Unit on that floor for the past two weeks. The patient’s room is adjacent to Besigye’s. Human rights lawyer Eron Kiiza, who first publicised the detention, said security personnel later claimed Mukose had been sent by activist Ingrid Turinawe to spy on them. Turinawe dismissed the allegation as laughable. Mukose was held at Mulago Police Station for more than 20 hours before his release. Police charged him in connection with being on the restricted floor. Besigye remains under tight security at the hospital after collapsing in court last week and being admitted to intensive care. Access to the floor has been heavily restricted. The incident has drawn criticism from opposition figures who say it reflects excessive security around the veteran politician. King Musah Media will continue monitoring developments around Besigye’s condition and hospital access. Teaser:

Dr Moses Mukose has been released on bond after being arrested and held overnight for “wandering” near Dr Kizza Besigye’s tightly guarded ward at Mulago Hospital. He says he was only visiting his father-in-law.

title: Bamasaba Kick Off 2026 Imbalu Cultural Festival at Mutoto as Nambeshe Calls for Unity and Development
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The 2026 Imbalu Cultural Festival was officially launched at Mutoto Cultural Grounds in Mbale City. NUP Acting President and Manjiya MP John Baptist Nambeshe attended and urged the Bamasaba community to unite for development while celebrating their biennial rite of passage to manhood.
image_alt: Scenes from the 2026 Imbalu Cultural Festival launch at Mutoto Cultural Grounds in Mbale
content: The Bamasaba community has officially launched the 2026 Imbalu Cultural Festival at the Mutoto Cultural Grounds in Mbale City. The event marks the start of the biennial traditional circumcision season, one of the most cherished rites of passage to manhood among the Bamasaba. The season is expected to run across clans in the Bugisu region until December. NUP Acting President and Manjiya County MP John Baptist Nambeshe attended the launch. In his remarks, he called on the community to unite and focus on development alongside the cultural celebrations. The launch featured traditional music, dance, and the initiation of candidates, drawing large crowds to the historic Mutoto site. Leaders and cultural figures present emphasised the importance of preserving the heritage while strengthening community bonds. Imbalu remains a central identity marker for the Bamasaba, combining ritual, celebration and social responsibility. Organisers and local leaders have stressed the need for safe and orderly observances throughout the season. King Musah Media will continue following the 2026 Imbalu activities across Bugisu.

title: Leaked Video Showing Frail Sam Mugumya Reignites Outrage Over Enforced Disappearances
author: Musanya Musa
excerpt: A video shared by NUP leader Robert Kyagulanyi (Bobi Wine) purporting to show long-missing opposition activist Sam Mugumya has triggered fresh national and international concern. The footage depicts a frail Mugumya using a walking frame. Security agencies have previously denied holding him.
image_alt: Still from leaked video of Sam Mugumya
content: A video circulated by National Unity Platform leader Robert Kyagulanyi, also known as Bobi Wine, has intensified demands for answers over the fate of opposition activist Sam Mugumya. In the post on 31 July 2026, Bobi Wine described the clip as leaked from an unknown detention facility. It shows Mugumya appearing frail and unable to walk without a walking frame. Bobi Wine called it evidence of torture and accused the government of continued denials about his whereabouts. Mugumya, a longtime aide to Dr Kizza Besigye and linked to the People’s Front for Freedom, was reportedly seized on 26 August 2025 from a hotel in Mbarara by armed men in military uniform and plain clothes. Eyewitnesses spoke of a coordinated operation involving a “drone” vehicle. The UPDF and police have consistently denied holding him. In responses to a habeas corpus application, security agencies told court that searches of detention facilities found no record of Mugumya. High Court Justice Collins Acellam earlier ordered his production, but the state maintained it had no knowledge of his location. Nearly a year later, there is still no official confirmation of his whereabouts or condition. The video’s authenticity has not been independently verified by mainstream media or official investigators. No security agency has publicly responded to the specific footage. Opposition figures and human rights advocates link the case to a wider pattern of alleged incommunicado detentions, pointing to recent incidents such as the re-arrest and temporary disappearance of NUP’s Muhammad Muwanga Kivumbi. Government officials have typically described such operations as responses to security threats and rejected claims of systematic abuse. Family, supporters and groups including the Uganda Law Society continue to demand that Mugumya be produced before a competent court, granted medical care if in custody, and that unacknowledged detentions end. Uganda’s Constitution and international conventions require prompt court appearance and access to lawyers for any detained person.

title: IGG Directs Immediate Interdiction of Chris Obore and Six Senior Parliament Officials Over Corruption
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Inspector General of Government Lady Justice Naluzze Aisha Batala has directed the Clerk to Parliament to immediately interdict Chris Obore and six other senior officials currently facing corruption charges. The order takes effect while their cases remain before the Anti-Corruption Court.
image_alt: IGG leader to paliament
content: The Inspector General of Government, Lady Justice Naluzze Aisha Batala, has ordered the immediate interdiction of seven senior Parliament officials facing corruption charges. In a directive issued on Friday, the IGG instructed Clerk to Parliament Adolf Mwesige to suspend Chris Ariko Obore, Director of Communications and Public Affairs, together with six others. The officials are Daniel Adilo (Director of Human Resource), Rajab Kaaya Ssemalulu (Principal Research Officer), Okwi Emmanuel Emuron (Principal Protocol Officer), Vincent Otebata (Capacity Development Officer), Leonard Okema (Executive Secretary, Office of the Speaker), and Stella Itute (Office Supervisor, Office of the Sergeant-at-Arms). The seven were arraigned before the Anti-Corruption Court on 1 July 2026 and charged with embezzlement and causing financial loss. They remain on remand at Luzira Prison.

The IGG stated that public interest requires the officials to step aside from their duties while the criminal proceedings continue. The directive is grounded in Article 230 of the Constitution and Section 13(6) of the Inspectorate of Government Act.  According to court documents, the group is accused of diverting public funds between 2023 and May 2026, with the alleged financial loss running into tens of billions of shillings.  The Inspectorate emphasised that the interdiction is necessary to protect the integrity of Parliament and uphold due process.  King Musah Media will continue following the court proceedings and Parliament’s response to the IGG directive.

title: Kyambogo University Under Fire Over Wrong Certificates Awarded to Graduates
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Kyambogo University has come under scrutiny after Members of Parliament discovered that some graduates were awarded certificates for courses they never studied. The revelation emerged during a session of the Parliamentary Committee on Education and Sports. Lawmakers heard that students admitted for programmes leading to Diplomas in Physical Education and Sports instead received certificates in Sports Management
image_alt: kyambongo university leadership befre the committe
content: Kampala, Uganda — Kyambogo University has come under scrutiny after Members of Parliament discovered that some graduates were awarded certificates for courses they never studied. The revelation emerged during a session of the Parliamentary Committee on Education and Sports. Lawmakers heard that students admitted for programmes leading to Diplomas in Physical Education and Sports instead received certificates in Sports Management.

Vice Chancellor Prof Justus Kwetegyeka appeared before the committee and acknowledged the anomaly. He told MPs that the university is already taking steps to correct the error through its standard internal processes.
<strong>Details of the Anomaly

According to information presented to the committee, the mix-up occurred in the awarding of diplomas. Students who enrolled and completed studies under the Physical Education and Sports curriculum were issued credentials for Sports Management — a related but distinct programme.Such errors raise serious questions about quality assurance, academic records management, and the integrity of university certificates. Affected graduates may face challenges when seeking employment, further studies, or professional registration, as their official documents do not accurately reflect the courses they completed.
<strong>University Response

Prof Kwetegyeka assured the committee that the institution is addressing the matter. The university has initiated corrective procedures, which typically involve verification of academic records, possible re-issuance of accurate certificates, and internal reviews to prevent similar occurrences in the future.The Vice Chancellor emphasised that the process is being handled according to established university regulations and academic standards.
<strong>Broader Concerns

This incident adds to ongoing discussions about administrative efficiency and academic standards in public universities. MPs on the Education and Sports Committee are expected to demand clearer timelines for the correction of certificates and stronger systems to avoid future errors.For the affected students and their families, the issue has caused frustration and uncertainty. Accurate certification is critical for career progression, especially in specialised fields such as sports education and management.King Musah Media will continue following developments as Kyambogo University works to resolve the certificate discrepancies and as Parliament monitors the corrective measures.

title: Kabaka Mutebi II Marks 33 Years on the Throne as Buganda Celebrates Amatikkira33 in Style at Watoto Church
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Buganda Kingdom on Friday staged a colourful and historic thanksgiving service to mark the 33rd coronation anniversary of His Majesty Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II, drawing thousands of subjects, cultural leaders, government officials, opposition figures, and religious leaders to Watoto Church in Bweyogerere.
image_alt: Cutting cake at Amattikira
content: Bweyogerere, Wakiso — Buganda Kingdom on Friday staged a colourful and historic thanksgiving service to mark the 33rd coronation anniversary of His Majesty Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II, drawing thousands of subjects, cultural leaders, government officials, opposition figures, and religious leaders to Watoto Church in Bweyogerere.The #Amatikkira33 celebrations, held for the first time at an evangelical church, highlighted the Kabaka’s enduring leadership, the kingdom’s cultural vibrancy, and growing inter-faith and inter-political unity around traditional institutions. Kabaka Mutebi II ascended the throne on 31 July 1993 at Naggalabi Buddo, restoring the Buganda monarchy after decades of abolition. Over the past 33 years, he has guided the kingdom through restoration, development initiatives, and advocacy on land, education, health, and youth empowerment.
<strong>High-Profile Attendance Underscores Unity

The service attracted a broad spectrum of leaders. Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja represented the central government, while Leader of Opposition Joel Ssenyonyi also attended, signalling cross-party respect for the Kabaka. Nnabagereka Sylvia Nagginda arrived in elegant traditional attire, drawing warm applause from the congregation. Katikkiro Charles Peter Mayiga and other kingdom officials led the royal delegation. Religious leaders from various denominations, including Pastor Martin Ssempa whose distinctive attire captured attention, joined the prayers and thanksgiving.President Yoweri Museveni sent a message of goodwill, hailing the Kabaka’s leadership and extending best wishes on the milestone anniversary.
<strong>Watoto Church Hosts Landmark Service and Supports Kingdom Project

Watoto Church, under Senior Pastor Julius Rwotlonyo, hosted the main thanksgiving for the first time — a significant gesture of inter-denominational harmony. The church presented a contribution of Shs 38 million towards the Kabaka’s Floating Clinic initiative, aimed at delivering medical services to the Ssese Islands and other hard-to-reach lake communities.The service featured prayers for the Kabaka’s continued good health and wisdom, traditional and contemporary music, poetry tributes, and messages of loyalty from subjects. Artist King Saha and poet Dr Irene Esther Mutuzo were among those who offered cultural performances and spoken-word pieces.
<strong>A Reign Defined by Stability and Development

Observers note that Kabaka Mutebi II’s 33-year reign has been marked by relative calm, institutional rebuilding, and practical programmes through the kingdom’s structures. Initiatives in education (including scholarships), health, agriculture, and environmental conservation have touched millions of lives across Buganda and beyond.The choice of Watoto Church as this year’s venue was widely praised as reflecting the Kabaka’s inclusive approach — welcoming all faiths while remaining rooted in Buganda’s cultural heritage.
<strong>Looking Ahead

As the Amatikkira33 celebrations continue with various community activities across the kingdom, focus remains on the Kabaka’s vision for a prosperous, peaceful, and culturally grounded Buganda. Subjects used the occasion to reaffirm their loyalty with the traditional cry of “Kabaka Awangaale!”King Musah Media congratulates His Majesty Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II on this historic milestone. May the next chapter of his reign bring even greater progress and unity.Long live the Kabaka!

title: LoP Joel Ssenyonyi Joins Buganda Kingdom Thanksgiving for Kabaka Mutebi II’s 33rd Coronation Anniversary
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Bweyogerere, Uganda — Leader of Opposition Joel Ssenyonyi on Friday attended a special thanksgiving service at Watoto Church in Bweyogerere to mark the 33rd anniversary of the coronation of Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II of Buganda. Ssenyonyi joined other political, cultural, and religious leaders in honouring the Kabaka’s three decades on the throne, a milestone symbolising unity, cultural resilience, and development within the kingdom.
image_alt: LoP at the 33rd Kabaka Coronation
content: Bweyogerere, Uganda — Leader of Opposition Joel Ssenyonyi on Friday attended a special thanksgiving service at Watoto Church in Bweyogerere to mark the 33rd anniversary of the coronation of Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II of Buganda. Ssenyonyi joined other political, cultural, and religious leaders in honouring the Kabaka’s three decades on the throne, a milestone symbolising unity, cultural resilience, and development within the kingdom.

Dressed formally, the LoP was seen engaging warmly with fellow attendees during the celebrations, reflecting the cross-aisle respect often extended to traditional institutions in Uganda’s political landscape.
<strong>Cross-Partisan Recognition of Cultural Heritage

The #Amatikkira33 events have drawn leaders from across the political divide, underscoring the unifying role of the Buganda Kingdom. Kabaka Mutebi II ascended the throne on July 31, 1993, and has since championed initiatives in education, healthcare, agriculture, and youth empowerment that benefit millions.Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja earlier represented the government at the same venue, highlighting cordial relations between the central government and the kingdom.
<strong>Broader Significance

Participation by opposition figures like Ssenyonyi demonstrates that cultural milestones often transcend partisan lines. The Kabaka’s reign has focused on restoring Buganda’s pride and advancing practical development programmes that complement national efforts.As celebrations continue across Buganda, the anniversary serves as a reminder of the important place traditional leaders occupy in Uganda’s social fabric. Subjects and observers have used the occasion to reaffirm loyalty to the Kabaka while praying for continued peace and progress.King Musah Media congratulates His Majesty Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II on this significant milestone. Long live the King!

title: PM Nabbanja Joins Buganda Kingdom for Historic #Amatikkira33 Celebrations at Watoto Church
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Bweyogerere, Uganda — Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja on Friday led government representation at Watoto Church in Bweyogerere as the Buganda Kingdom marked the 33rd anniversary of the coronation of Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II.
image_alt: Prime Minister reaching at watoto church for 33rd coronation
content: <strong>Bweyogerere, Uganda

— Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja on Friday led government representation at Watoto Church in Bweyogerere as the Buganda Kingdom marked the 33rd anniversary of the coronation of Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II.

The colourful #Amatikkira33 celebrations brought together cultural leaders, government officials, clergy, and thousands of Baganda subjects to honour the Kabaka’s enduring reign and contributions to peace, development, and cultural preservation in Uganda.

Dressed in traditional attire, PM Nabbanja was warmly received as she arrived for the commemorative service. The event highlighted the strong synergy between the central government and traditional institutions in fostering national unity and community development.
<strong>Significance of Amatikkira33

Kabaka Mutebi II ascended the throne on July 31, 1993, restoring the Buganda Kingdom’s cultural monarchy after years of abolition. Over the past 33 years, he has spearheaded numerous initiatives in education, health, agriculture, and youth empowerment through the kingdom’s structures, significantly impacting millions of subjects across Buganda and beyond.The anniversary celebrations serve as a moment of reflection on the Kabaka’s visionary leadership, which emphasises moral values, land stewardship, and harmonious coexistence. Watoto Church, known for its community outreach, provided a fitting venue for this year’s commemorative prayers and thanksgiving.
<strong>Excerpt:

“A strong cultural institution working hand in hand with government brings development closer to the people.” — Remarks from government sources during the Amatikkira33 event.Government-Kingdom PartnershipThe presence of the Prime Minister underscores the Museveni administration’s commitment to respecting and collaborating with Uganda’s traditional leaders. Buganda remains one of the most influential kingdoms, playing a key role in social mobilisation and service delivery.As the celebrations continue across Buganda, focus will turn to the Kabaka’s ongoing projects and the kingdom’s vision for the next phase of its restoration and growth. Subjects and well-wishers have used the occasion to express loyalty and gratitude to Kabaka Mutebi II for his steady guidance.King Musah Media extends congratulations to His Majesty the Kabaka on this milestone anniversary. Long live the King!

title: She Cranes Blaze Past Scotland! Uganda Delivers Dominant 65-56 Thrashing at Commonwealth Games
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Glasgow, Scotland — Uganda’s She Cranes delivered a commanding performance in netball as they defeated hosts Scotland 65-56 in a Pool B encounter at the Commonwealth Games. The win showcased the growing strength and tactical maturity of Ugandan women’s netball on the global stage.
image_alt: She Cranes performance in common wealth games
content: Glasgow, Scotland — Uganda’s She Cranes delivered a commanding performance in netball as they defeated hosts Scotland 65-56 in a Pool B encounter at the Commonwealth Games. The win showcased the growing strength and tactical maturity of Ugandan women’s netball on the global stage.

Playing with pace, precision, and defensive intensity, the She Cranes controlled large portions of the match against a resilient but fatigued Scottish side. Uganda’s attacking unit combined slick movement and accurate shooting, while their defence disrupted Scotland’s flow throughout the contest at the Hydro arena.This result adds to Uganda’s impressive run at the Games, following strong victories over Wales and Trinidad & Tobago. The She Cranes’ attacking flair and defensive organisation have been standout features, with the team posting a record 80-goal haul in an earlier match.Key Highlights from the Match  Uganda maintained pressure from the opening whistle, building leads through coordinated play.
Scotland fought back in patches, showing home determination, but struggled to contain Uganda’s attacking threats.
The She Cranes’ bench contributed effectively, ensuring momentum never wavered significantly.
<strong>Uganda’s Rising Star in Netball

The She Cranes’ success reflects years of investment in women’s sport in Uganda. Netball has gained significant popularity, with domestic leagues and grassroots programmes producing talented athletes capable of competing at the highest level.This victory not only boosts Uganda’s medal prospects but also inspires young girls across the country to take up the sport. President Museveni and sports officials have consistently highlighted the importance of women’s achievements in elevating national pride.Head coach and technical team will now focus on recovery and preparation for remaining fixtures, aiming to progress deep into the knockout stages and challenge traditional powerhouses like Australia, New Zealand, and Jamaica.Proud
<strong>Moment for Ugandan Sports

Uganda’s women continue to shine at these Games — from netball triumphs to historic medals in other disciplines. The She Cranes’ performance against Scotland epitomises resilience, skill, and national spirit.Congratulations to the entire squad and technical bench. Uganda is making its mark in Glasgow!

title: President Museveni Hosts UK MP to Strengthen Uganda-UK Healthcare Partnership
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni on Thursday welcomed Hon. Beccy Cooper MP, Chair of the UK All-Party Parliamentary Group on Global Health, for discussions focused on deepening bilateral ties in the health sector.
image_alt: President Museveni in a meeting with Mp from Uk
content: Kampala, Uganda — President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni on Thursday welcomed Hon. Beccy Cooper MP, Chair of the UK All-Party Parliamentary Group on Global Health, for discussions focused on deepening bilateral ties in the health sector.

The meeting centred on opportunities for collaboration in medical training, skills transfer, and enhancing overall health service delivery across Uganda. President Museveni used the occasion to brief the British lawmaker on Uganda’s successful containment and defeat of the recent Ebola outbreak, attributing the achievement to the dedication of Ugandan health workers and the robustness of the country’s response systems.
Excerpt:

“We discussed strengthening Uganda-UK collaboration in healthcare, particularly in medical training, skills transfer, and improving health service delivery. I also briefed her on Uganda’s successful defeat of the recent Ebola outbreak...” — President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni.
<strong>Building on Existing Ties

Uganda and the United Kingdom have long partnered in health initiatives, including support for infrastructure, training programmes, and disease surveillance. This latest engagement underscores continued interest in leveraging UK expertise to address Uganda’s health priorities such as workforce development and emergency preparedness.The President’s emphasis on the Ebola success highlights lessons learned in rapid response, community engagement, and coordination — areas where international partnerships have proven valuable in past outbreaks.Hon. Cooper’s role in the All-Party Parliamentary Group positions her as a key advocate for global health issues within the UK Parliament. Such visits often pave the way for increased funding, technical assistance, or policy alignment between the two nations.
<strong>Looking Ahead

As Uganda continues to strengthen its healthcare system, partnerships like this could accelerate progress toward universal health coverage and resilience against future health threats. Stakeholders in the sector will be keen to see concrete follow-ups from the discussions, including potential new training exchanges or joint programmes.

title: Lira District Officials Jailed Four Years Each for Land Fraud and Abuse of Office
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: “The three public officials were each sentenced to four years’ imprisonment and will not hold any public office for the next 10 years, while Atoo Rebecca was sentenced to one year in prison.” — Anti-Corruption Unit statement.
image_alt: lira Officials Sentenced
content: Lira District Officials Jailed Four Years Each for Land Fraud and Abuse of Office By Senior Correspondent, King Musah Media Kampala, Uganda — The Anti-Corruption Division of the High Court has convicted and sentenced three public officials from Lira District Local Government to four years’ imprisonment each for their roles in a fraudulent land scheme that targeted district property. A private individual linked to the scam received a one-year sentence.

The convicted persons are Opio Francis (District Staff Surveyor), Otike Pabius (District Natural Resources Officer), Ogwanga Joel (Cartographer at the Ministry of Lands, Lira Zonal Office), and Atoo Rebecca (sister to Opio Francis, in whose name the land was fraudulently registered). The court also barred the three public servants from holding any public office for the next 10 years.
<strong>Details of the Fraud

Between February and August 2019, Lira District initiated the process to obtain a certificate of title for its land at Ireda Estate. According to the prosecution, Opio and Otike deliberately excluded a portion of the land during surveying. With assistance from Ogwanga, they allegedly procured a Freehold Certificate of Title for Plot 3–5 Ben Emor Road, Ireda Estate, and registered it in Atoo Rebecca’s name.Atoo later sold the land to buyer Olam Pius, with all the accused participating in or witnessing the transaction. The State House Anti-Corruption Unit, working with the Criminal Investigations Directorate (CID) and the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP), arraigned the suspects in June 2023.The court found them guilty of Abuse of Office, Fraudulent Procurement of a Certificate of Title, and Conspiracy to Defraud.
Excerpt:

“The three public officials were each sentenced to four years’ imprisonment and will not hold any public office for the next 10 years, while Atoo Rebecca was sentenced to one year in prison.” — Anti-Corruption Unit statement.
<strong>Significance of the Ruling

This conviction sends a strong message against the misuse of official positions to alienate public land, a persistent challenge in many Ugandan districts. Land-related corruption often deprives communities of resources meant for public services such as schools, health centres, or infrastructure.The Anti-Corruption Unit praised the collaboration between agencies and urged citizens to report suspicious activities. Questions remain among observers about whether the district has recovered the land and if the buyer, Olam Pius, has received any compensation or redress.Such cases underscore the importance of transparency in land management and the role of anti-graft bodies in recovering public assets. King Musah Media will continue monitoring developments, including any appeals or asset recovery efforts.

title: Anti-Corruption Court Remands OPM Commissioner and IT Officer Over Alleged Abuse of Office
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: “The prosecution of the two officials underscores the IGG’s unwavering resolve to combat corruption and abuse of public office.” — Inspectorate of Government statement.
image_alt: OPM Officials taken to court
content: Kampala, Uganda — The Anti-Corruption Court has remanded two senior officials from the Office of the Prime Minister (OPM) — Commissioner for Refugees Management Patrick Okello and Assistant Information Technology Officer Noel Ikwap — to Luzira Prison on charges of abuse of office.

The pair appeared before Grade One Magistrate Esther Asiimwe on Thursday, where the court ordered their remand until August 10, 2026, for case mention and hearing of their bail applications. The charges were instituted by the Inspectorate of Government (IGG), which is leading the prosecution.The IGG team, including Principal Officer Prosecutions Mikka Luteete, Principal Officer Litigation Diana Nantabazi, and Inspectorate Officer Pius Kaweesi, represented the anti-graft body in court. According to the IGG, the case forms part of its ongoing efforts to enforce accountability and the rule of law in public service management.
<strong>Excerpt:
“The prosecution of the two officials underscores the IGG’s unwavering resolve to combat corruption and abuse of public office.” — Inspectorate of Government statement.
<strong>Context of the Case

The Office of the Prime Minister plays a pivotal role in coordinating government business, including the management of refugees and disaster preparedness. Allegations of abuse of office in such departments often centre on procurement irregularities, fund mismanagement, or unauthorised use of public resources — issues that have previously drawn scrutiny in Uganda’s refugee response programmes.This development comes amid the IGG’s continued high-profile operations targeting public officials. Both suspects are presumed innocent until proven guilty, and the court will hear their side of the story during bail proceedings and the full trial.
<strong>Broader Implications

The remand highlights the judiciary and anti-corruption agencies’ active role in addressing governance challenges within key ministries. Supporters of the IGG view such actions as essential for restoring public trust in institutions handling significant donor and government funds, particularly in humanitarian sectors.Critics sometimes argue that selective prosecutions may occur without deeper systemic reforms. Regardless, the case will be closely watched by civil society, development partners, and the public for its outcome and any potential revelations about operations at OPM.

title: Parliament Vets Juma Witonze Kisekka as New Minister of State for Internal Affairs
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Uganda’s Parliament Appointments Committee has successfully vetted Hon. Juma Witonze Kisekka, President Yoweri Museveni’s nominee for Minister of State for Internal Affairs. The process, completed on Thursday morning, paves the way for his formal appointment following a swift review of his credentials.
image_alt: Paliament Vetting
content: Kampala, Uganda

Uganda’s Parliament Appointments Committee has successfully vetted Hon. Juma Witonze Kisekka, President Yoweri Museveni’s nominee for Minister of State for Internal Affairs. The process, completed on Thursday morning, paves the way for his formal appointment following a swift review of his credentials.

Chaired by Speaker Jacob Oboth Oboth, the committee included Deputy Speaker Thomas Tayebwa and other lawmakers. They examined Kisekka’s documents and suitability for the sensitive internal security docket.
