With no major issues raised, the panel will now submit its report to the President, who nominated him three days ago. Kisekka is expected to be sworn in soon after presidential assent.
<strong>Background and Political Context

Kisekka, a dedicated National Resistance Movement (NRM) figure and Chief Coordinator of the Patriotic League of Uganda (PLU) for the Greater Mpigi region, hails from Gomba. His nomination comes after Parliament rejected an earlier candidate, Dr Lawrence Muganga, primarily over unresolved questions regarding multiple citizenships and documentation.The Internal Affairs docket is critical in Uganda, overseeing police, immigration, prisons, and overall internal security. Observers view Kisekka’s selection as a strategic move to install an experienced loyalist with diplomatic and grassroots mobilisation credentials.During the session, committee members probed Kisekka on his vision for the ministry, governance experience, and plans to address key challenges such as public safety and border management. Sources close to the process described the vetting as thorough yet cordial, reflecting the committee’s mandate under parliamentary rules.Kisekka expressed gratitude for the opportunity, reaffirming his commitment to national service. His approval is widely expected to sail through given the ruling party’s dominance in the Appointments Committee.
<strong>Implications for Cabinet and Governance

This development continues Museveni’s pattern of timely cabinet adjustments to maintain stability within the executive. It also highlights Parliament’s oversight role, as demonstrated by the earlier rejection of Muganga — a rare instance of the legislature pushing back on a presidential nomination.For the Greater Mpigi area and broader central region, Kisekka’s elevation strengthens local representation at the national level. Critics, however, may question the pace and depth of such appointments in addressing long-standing security and governance concerns.King Musah Media will monitor Kisekka’s swearing-in and early priorities in the Internal Affairs ministry.

title: Idi Amin’s Grandson Disqualified in Commonwealth Games Boxing Quarter-Final
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: “I might be the new King of Scotland. It’s possible... I have that dream that I’m gonna go back with gold medal. That’s the reason I’m here in Glasgow right now.” — Aziz Abdul (Ringo), ahead of the quarter-final.
image_alt: amin's son in the ring
content: Glasgow, Scotland — Ugandan super-heavyweight boxer Aziz Abdul, grandson of former military ruler Idi Amin, saw his medal ambitions end dramatically at the 2026 Commonwealth Games after he was disqualified for headbutting England’s Damar Thomas in their men’s 90+kg quarter-final.

Abdul, who fights under the nickname “Ringo,” received three warnings before referee intervention early in the third round on Wednesday. Trailing on the scorecards at the time of the stoppage, the 25-year-old Ugandan expressed strong dissatisfaction with the decision, suggesting bias and claiming an elbow from Thomas contributed to the head contact. Thomas advances to the semi-finals with at least a bronze medal guaranteed.

The bout had drawn significant attention due to Abdul’s family lineage. Idi Amin, who ruled Uganda from 1971 to 1979, was himself a noted boxer in his younger years, holding the national light-heavyweight title for nearly a decade. Abdul had spoken ambitiously ahead of the contest, expressing a desire to win gold in Glasgow — a city linked to his grandfather’s self-proclaimed “King of Scotland” title in the 1970s — and bring Uganda its first Commonwealth boxing medal since 1990.
<strong>A Story Beyond the Ring

Abdul had never met his grandfather, who died in exile in Saudi Arabia in 2003 when Abdul was a toddler. While acknowledging the complex legacy, the boxer has drawn inspiration from Amin’s sporting past rather than his controversial political rule, which is widely condemned for widespread human rights abuses.In the build-up, Abdul arrived in Scotland enthusiastic, even raising the Scottish flag and promising his powerful “Ringo punch” would deliver victory. His disqualification ends Uganda’s immediate medal hopes in boxing at these Games but highlights the growing profile of Ugandan talent on the international stage.Thomas, the home fighter, showed composure and effective boxing before the stoppage. He now eyes a place in the final as the tournament progresses at the Scottish Exhibition Centre.Uganda Boxing Federation officials and fans back home will no doubt review the officiating closely, while Abdul returns to Kampala with valuable experience from his debut Commonwealth Games appearance. The incident serves as a reminder of the fine margins and intense scrutiny in elite amateur boxing.King Musah Media will keep tracking African performances at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

title: Busoga University Reopening Delayed as Government Awaits Museveni’s Verdict on Name
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: “Some people wanted it to remain Busoga University, while others proposed Kiira University and other names. We have now concluded the consultations and are left with only one stakeholder, the President.” — Dr John Chrysostom Muyingo, Acting Minister of Education and Sports.
image_alt: Busoga University Building
content: Iganga, Uganda — Hopes for Busoga University to welcome students for the August 2026 intake have been put on hold. The Ugandan government is waiting for President Yoweri Museveni’s decision on the institution’s official name before completing the legal processes to establish it as a public university.

Physical infrastructure at the Iganga campus is ready after a major government-funded refurbishment valued at Shs 3.795 billion, executed by the UPDF Civil Engineers Brigade and handed over on July 20, 2026. The National Council for Higher Education (NCHE) has completed its inspection, yet bureaucratic steps — including the formation of a university council, appointment of management, and staff recruitment — remain pending.Acting Minister of Education and Sports, Dr John Chrysostom Muyingo, explained that stakeholder consultations on possible names, such as retaining “Busoga University” or adopting alternatives like “Kiira University,” have largely concluded. “We have now concluded the consultations and are left with only one stakeholder, the President,” he said. A transition task force has submitted its report seeking Museveni’s views. Once approved, the proposal will proceed to Cabinet and Parliament for a statutory instrument.
<strong>From Private Troubles to Public Ambition

Busoga University, founded in 1999 and affiliated with the Busoga Diocese of the Church of Uganda, faced significant challenges. It was closed in 2017 by the NCHE following investigations that revealed unqualified academic staff, unaccredited programmes, and the fraudulent award of degrees to more than 1,000 students, including many from South Sudan.In January 2018, President Museveni directed the Ministry of Education to take over both Busoga University and Mountains of the Moon University as public institutions. The Church of Uganda has supported the transition and retains ownership of over 200 acres of land at the site.Local leaders and church officials have welcomed the developments while urging speed. Iganga South MP Andrew Kaluya Namitego described the project as a long-held regional dream. “We are very happy that Busoga University is finally taking shape... We are fast-tracking the issue of the statutory instruments,” he noted.Rt Rev Patrick Wakula, Bishop of Busoga Central Diocese, expressed optimism: “It is my prayer that we begin as early as possible. We have gone through a lot of history, but even those institutions that have reached where they are today began with one step.” Prof John Tabuti, chairperson of the transition task force, appealed for continued stakeholder support.
<strong>Implications for Students and the Region

The delay means government-sponsored students for the new academic year have already been allocated to other public universities. Private admissions continue elsewhere, potentially affecting prospective students from Busoga and surrounding areas who were counting on local access to higher education.Critics may see the situation as emblematic of decision-making processes in Uganda that concentrate significant authority at the highest level. Supporters, however, point to the substantial public investment and the potential for a revitalised institution to drive regional development, create jobs, and expand access to quality tertiary education.Stakeholders from the Church, local MPs, and the task force remain hopeful that the remaining processes will be completed swiftly once the President’s input is received, allowing the university to open its doors in the near future.King Musah Media will continue to monitor developments as this important regional higher education project moves forward.

title: FORMER MP MUWANGA KIVUMBI ARRAIGNED IN COURT AFTER ABDUCTION CLAIMS
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Former Butambala County Member of Parliament Muhammad Muwanga Kivumbi has been charged with incitement to violence and remanded to prison after appearing before the Butambala Magistrates Court on Wednesday. The development follows his dramatic reappearance after over two weeks of being missing.
image_alt: Muwanga Kivumbi in court
content: Former Butambala County Member of Parliament Muhammad Muwanga Kivumbi has been charged with incitement to violence and remanded to prison after appearing before the Butambala Magistrates Court on Wednesday. The development follows his dramatic reappearance after over two weeks of being missing.ABDUCTION ON CAMERA AND OFFICIAL DENIALSKivumbi was reportedly intercepted in Mpigi on 9 July by police before armed men in military attire took him away. Video footage of the incident circulated widely on social media. Both the Uganda Police and the Uganda Peoples Defence Forces subsequently denied knowledge of his whereabouts or involvement in any abduction. The UPDF in particular filed an affidavit stating that checks in all gazetted detention facilities found no trace of the former legislator.His family and political allies raised alarm over the disappearance describing it as an enforced disappearance. A habeas corpus application was filed in the High Court prompting judicial directives for security agencies to produce him or explain his status.REAPPEARANCE AND COURT PROCEEDINGSKivumbi resurfaced when he was dropped off at Nateete Police Station by unknown operatives. He was then transferred and arraigned in Butambala where the court remanded him. The case has been adjourned to 11 August for further mention. Opposition leaders including those from the National Unity Platform have condemned the events as part of a pattern of political persecution and questioned the credibility of state institutions. They demand accountability for the period he was held incommunicado.BALANCED PERSPECTIVE ON RULE OF LAWSecurity agencies have not issued detailed public statements on the specific allegations of abduction. Judicial processes continue with the High Court scheduled to deliver a ruling on related applications soon. Legal experts emphasise the importance of due process transparency and protection of individual rights in such high profile matters regardless of political affiliation.The case continues to fuel public debate on issues of personal liberty state accountability and the administration of justice in Uganda.
King Musah Media will follow subsequent court appearances and provide factual updates.

title: JUDICIARY TIGHTENS MEDIA ACCESS RULES FOR BESIGYE TREASON CASE
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The Judiciary of Uganda has issued revised guidelines for the high profile treason trial of retired Colonel Kizza Besigye and two others. The new rules focus on security screening and access controls as the case resumes amid heightened public interest.
image_alt: Kizza Byesigye in court
content: The Judiciary of Uganda has issued revised guidelines for the high profile treason trial of retired Colonel Kizza Besigye and two others. The new rules focus on security screening and access controls as the case resumes amid heightened public interest.DETAILS OF REVISED GUIDELINESUnder the updated measures all media equipment including cameras audio recorders laptops and other electronic devices must undergo mandatory security screening before entry into the court premises. Requests for live broadcasts of proceedings require prior submission to the Public Relations Office for approval. These steps come as the trial faces continued scrutiny over procedural matters and public access.CONTEXT OF THE ONGOING TRIALThe guidelines were announced as Besigye appeared in court where he later collapsed leading to suspension of proceedings. The accused has objected to proceeding without his chosen lawyers citing the arrest of his lead counsel and the denial of entry to Kenyan lawyer Martha Karua. The case which has run since last year without bail granted to Besigye continues to draw political attention.REACTIONS AND CONCERNSSupporters of Besigye and some legal observers argue that the restrictions could limit transparency and the constitutional right to a public trial. Others including judicial officials maintain that the measures are necessary for security order and protection of witnesses in a sensitive matter.President Museveni has previously stated that delays in the trial stem from actions by the accused rather than the courts. The opposition views the process as politically driven.IMPLICATIONS FOR PUBLIC INTERESTThe tightened rules have sparked debate on balancing judicial security needs with the principles of open justice in Uganda. As Besigye receives medical care following his court collapse questions persist about the trial timeline and the health of the accused.King Musah Media remains committed to providing factual and balanced coverage of this developing story.

title: DR KIZZA BESIGYE COLLAPSES IN COURT AS TREASON TRIAL DRAGS ON
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Retired Colonel Kizza Besigye was rushed to hospital on Wednesday after he fainted in the High Court during his ongoing treason trial. Court proceedings were immediately suspended. The incident has once again thrown the spotlight on the prolonged legal battle and the political tensions surrounding the opposition veteran.
image_alt: Kizza Byesigye collapses in court
content: Retired Colonel Kizza Besigye was rushed to hospital on Wednesday after he fainted in the High Court during his ongoing treason trial. Court proceedings were immediately suspended. The incident has once again thrown the spotlight on the prolonged legal battle and the political tensions surrounding the opposition veteran.HEALTH DETERIORATION IN CUSTODYBesigye who has been in detention since his arrest last year collapsed while objecting to the continuation of the trial without his preferred legal team. Eyewitness accounts and video footage from the courtroom show the accused man protesting the appointment of state lawyers by Justice Emmanuel Baguma before he fell ill. Prison officers had handcuffed him and surrounded him as the session continued.Medical sources indicate that Besigye has faced health challenges while in custody. His supporters argue that the extended detention without bail has contributed to his deteriorating condition.LONG TRIAL AND LEGAL HURDLESThe treason case against Besigye and his co-accused has stretched for months with repeated delays. The opposition leader and his allies maintain that the charges are politically motivated. Critics of the process point to the arrest of his lead counsel and the denial of entry into Uganda for Kenyan lawyer and former Justice Minister Martha Karua who was expected to join the defence team.The judiciary has defended its handling of the matter citing security concerns and procedural requirements including new guidelines on court access that limited observers and journalists.PRESIDENTIAL REMARKS ON DELAYSPresident Yoweri Museveni has publicly stated that Besigye himself is responsible for the slow pace of the trial rather than the courts. The President described the situation as one where the accused employs tactics to prolong proceedings. Opposition voices reject this view and accuse the state of using the justice system to sideline political rivals.BALANCED CALLS FOR RESOLUTIONLegal experts and human rights observers have called for a fair and expeditious hearing that respects due process and the right to legal representation of choice. As Besigye receives medical attention questions remain about his fitness to stand trial and the broader implications for Uganda's political landscape.King Musah Media will continue monitoring the case and provide balanced updates as developments unfold.

title: BUGANDA RELEASES NEW ARRANGEMENT OF NATIONAL ANTHEM
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The Katikkiro of Buganda  Charles Peter Mayiga  has officially released a refreshed version of the kingdom's national anthem  Ekitiibwa kya Buganda. The announcement came through a post on X today  featuring a performance by the St. Charles Lwanga Lubaga Cathedral Choir.
image_alt: Katikiro Charles Peter Mayiga
content: The Katikkiro of Buganda Charles Peter Mayiga has officially released a refreshed version of the kingdom's national anthem Ekitiibwa kya Buganda. The announcement came through a post on X today featuring a performance by the St. Charles Lwanga Lubaga Cathedral Choir.TRADITION MEETS PROFESSIONAL ARRANGEMENTComposed in 1939 by Rev. Polycarp Kakooza the anthem known in English as The Pride of Buganda holds deep significance for the people of Buganda. The new edition was arranged by music experts and rendered entirely in the Luganda language. It showcases the full vocal range of the choir with clear soprano alto tenor and bass sections supported by keyboards saxophone and traditional drums.Mayiga described the project as an effort to preserve and promote Buganda's cultural heritage through high quality production. The video performance recorded outdoors with the choir in coordinated attire highlights both musical excellence and cultural pride.POSITIVE RECEPTION FROM THE PUBLICEarly reactions on social media have been largely favorable. Users praised the improved pronunciations harmonious delivery and overall production quality. Several commenters requested that the anthem be made available on digital platforms such as Spotify and iTunes to allow wider access and international reach.This release comes at a time when cultural institutions across Uganda continue to explore ways to keep traditional expressions relevant for younger generations while maintaining their authenticity.LOOKING AHEAD FOR BUGANDAKingdom officials have not yet detailed further plans for distribution or additional cultural projects. However the initiative underscores ongoing efforts to strengthen Buganda's identity within the broader national context.King Musah Media will continue to monitor developments and provide updates on this and other stories of cultural importance.

title: Nation Media Group Uganda Cleared to Resume Operations After June Shutdown
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: In a significant development for media freedom in Uganda, Nation Media Group (NMG) Uganda, publishers of Daily Monitor and operators of NTV Uganda and other platforms  has been cleared to resume full operations following a government-mandated shutdown in June 2026.
image_alt: letter showing Ntv is allowed to operate
content: In a significant development for media freedom in Uganda, Nation Media Group (NMG) Uganda publishers of Daily Monitor and operators of NTV Uganda and other platforms, has been cleared to resume full operations following a government-mandated shutdown in June 2026.

The announcement, which has sparked widespread reactions across social media, marks the end of a tense period that raised concerns about press freedom, regulatory compliance, and the role of independent media in the country.
<strong>What We Know So Far
NMG Uganda’s outlets, including the influential Daily Monitor newspaper and NTV television, were taken off air and out of circulation in June.
The clearance to resume comes directly from relevant authorities, allowing the group to restart broadcasting, printing, and digital operations.
As of Tuesday, July 28, 2026, the public is already celebrating the return of a major independent voice, with many expressing relief and high expectations for robust journalism.

image_alt: Jumah watenga

The move comes amid ongoing government efforts to strengthen internal security, immigration management, and overall governance in a key ministry that oversees critical functions including police, prisons, immigration, and disaster preparedness.
Who is Hon. Juma Witonze Kisekka?

He has been associated with party structures and grassroots mobilization efforts. The appointment has drawn mixed immediate reactions online Ã¢ÂÂ congratulations from supporters who see it as recognition of loyalty and mobilization work, alongside questions from others about the naming (Witonze/Kisekka) and implications for the Internal Affairs docket.Significance of the Internal Affairs MinistryThe Ministry of Internal Affairs is one of UgandaÃ¢ÂÂs most strategic portfolios. Immigration and refugee management.
Citizenship and passports.

Prisons and correctional services.

Ultimately, performance in office Ã¢ÂÂ transparency, effectiveness in maintaining security without compromising rights, and efficient service delivery Ã¢ÂÂ will shape public perception.Balanced OutlookOpportunities: A new appointee can bring renewed vigor, fresh ideas on community policing, digital immigration systems, or enhanced coordination among security agencies. If Hon. Witonze leverages his mobilization experience effectively, he could strengthen government-citizen linkages on security matters.Challenges: The ministry demands high competence in complex areas like human rights balancing, corruption control within security organs, and diplomatic handling of cross-border issues. title: Police Urge Peace and Order as Uganda Prepares for Local Council Elections Today
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: With campaigns closed yesterday (Monday, July 27, 2026) and voting scheduled for today Tuesday, July 28, 2026, the Uganda Police Force has issued a strong public reminder to candidates, their supporters, and the general public to uphold peace, lawfulness, and order throughout the Local Council (LC) elections.
image_alt: Police Urguing Ugandans On Elections
content: With campaigns closed yesterday (Monday, July 27, 2026) and voting scheduled for Today, July 28, 2026, the Uganda Police Force has issued a strong public reminder to candidates, their supporters, and the general public to uphold peace, lawfulness, and order throughout the Local Council (LC) elections.

In a statement shared on their official X account, police spokesperson and other security stakeholders emphasized zero tolerance for any form of misconduct that could undermine the integrity of the electoral process. The message comes at a critical moment when grassroots leadership positions — vital for local governance, dispute resolution, and community development — are up for grabs across the country.Context of the Local Council ElectionsLocal Council elections in Uganda represent one of the most decentralized and community-driven aspects of the country’s democratic system. LC positions, from village (LC1) to higher local levels, play key roles in everyday governance: mobilizing communities for development projects, maintaining local security, resolving minor disputes, and linking citizens with higher government structures.These elections often see high participation because they directly affect people’s daily lives. However, they can also be intense due to personal rivalries, clan or religious influences, resource competition, and occasional political alignments with national parties. Past cycles have occasionally witnessed voter bribery, intimidation, vote rigging allegations, violence, and disputes over voter registers or candidate eligibility.Police Message: A Call to ResponsibilityThe police statement, attributed in part to @mkituuma
, stresses that:T<em>he electoral process must remain peaceful, lawful, and orderly.
All forms of misconduct — including violence, hate speech, voter intimidation, destruction of campaign materials, or any acts that disrupt voting — will not be tolerated.
Security and administrative teams are deployed and vigilant to ensure smooth proceedings.

This proactive communication aligns with standard pre-election security protocols. It serves both as a deterrent and a reassurance to voters that authorities are monitoring the situation closely.Broader Picture: Opportunities and ChallengesPositive Aspects:Grassroots elections strengthen local democracy and give ordinary citizens a direct say in who leads their villages and parishes.
High turnout can enhance accountability, as local leaders are often more accessible than national politicians.
Peaceful polls would reflect maturing democratic norms at the community level.
Potential Risks:In some areas, competition can turn personal or ethnic, leading to tensions.
Logistical challenges such as inadequate voting materials, voter register inaccuracies, or accessibility issues in remote regions sometimes arise.
Economic pressures may tempt candidates or agents into vote-buying or other malpractices.
Misinformation on social media or through word-of-mouth can inflame unnecessary conflicts.

Security forces, the Electoral Commission, and civil society organizations typically collaborate during such exercises to address these issues in real time.A Balanced Call to ActionFor a successful election, responsibility lies with multiple stakeholders:Candidates: Campaign on issues (service delivery, local development, integrity) rather than personal attacks. Concede gracefully where defeated and pursue disputes through legal channels.
Supporters and Voters: Exercise democratic rights responsibly — vote peacefully, respect differing choices, and avoid provocation.
Security Agencies: Enforce the law impartially, without bias toward any side.
Electoral Commission: Ensure transparency, timely resolution of complaints, and credible results.
Media and Civil Society: Report factually and promote peace messaging.

Uganda has made notable progress in managing elections with reduced large-scale violence in recent cycles, though isolated incidents remain a concern. Tomorrow’s polls offer another opportunity to demonstrate maturity in local democratic practice.As voting begins, King Musah Media urges all Ugandans to prioritize peace and national unity. Let the voice of the people prevail in an atmosphere of calm and fairness. The eyes of the nation and the world will be on how communities conduct themselves during this important grassroots democratic exercise.Stay safe, vote wisely, and may the best leaders emerge for the service of their communities.
We will monitor developments and provide updates on the conduct and outcomes of the July 28, 2026 Local Council elections.

title: Police Intensify Crackdown on Illegal Charcoal Trade in West Nile: Eight Suspects Arrested as Environmental Protection Efforts Gain Momentum
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: In a decisive joint operation, Uganda Police Forces Environmental Protection Police Unit (EPPU), working alongside the Uganda Peoples Defence Forces (UPDF) and the National Forestry Authority (NFA), has arrested eight suspects in Madi Okollo District and surrounding areas of the West Nile sub-region for illegal dealing in charcoal. The operation, conducted on July 25, 2026, resulted in the impoundment of 72 bags of charcoal, now secured as exhibits at Madi Okollo Police Station.
image_alt: Police Media Brief
content: In a decisive joint operation, Uganda Police Forces Environmental Protection Police Unit (EPPU), working alongside the Uganda PeopleÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂs Defence Forces (UPDF) and the National Forestry Authority (NFA), has arrested eight suspects in Madi Okollo District and surrounding areas of the West Nile sub-region for illegal dealing in charcoal. The operation, conducted on July 25, 2026, resulted in the impoundment of 72 bags of charcoal, now secured as exhibits at Madi Okollo Police Station. The suspects face charges of illegal dealing in forest produce, in direct contravention of the law and a presidential directive

This latest enforcement action underscores a sustained government campaign to combat environmental degradation in Northern Uganda, where unchecked charcoal production and trade continue to threaten forest ecosystems, livelihoods, and long-term climate resilience.
Presidential Directive and Legal Backdrop

In May 2023, President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni issued Executive Order No. 3 of 2023on environmental protection. The order explicitly bans the burning, production, transportation, and commercial trade of charcoal across Northern and North Eastern Uganda, including the sub-regions of Karamoja, Teso, Lango, Acholi, and West Nile. The measure aims to curb rampant deforestation driven by commercial charcoal activities.

Police have warned that such activities are criminal and will be met with firm prosecution. Joint agencies vow to maintain operations, impound exhibits, and encourage public reporting of illegal forest exploitation.
Similar operations in recent months have netted dozens more suspects and thousands of bags of charcoal across Northern Uganda, signaling a broader push against environmental offenders.
The Environmental Crisis Driving the Crackdown

Charcoal production in Uganda, particularly in woodland and savanna regions like West Nile, has long been linked to significant deforestation. Trees are felled, carbonized in traditional earth kilns (often inefficient and smoky), and sold as a primary cooking fuel for urban and rural households. While charcoal provides energy and income for many, the scale of unregulated commercial production accelerates forest loss, soil erosion, biodiversity decline, and contributes to climate change through carbon emissions.

In Northern Uganda, where vegetation recovery can be slower due to climatic conditions and human pressures (including refugee settlements and agricultural expansion), experts have raised alarms about desertification risks. Streams drying up, reduced wildlife habitats, and declining agricultural productivity are among the reported consequences. The government views the ban in designated areas as a necessary intervention to allow forest regeneration while promoting alternatives like efficient cookstoves, briquettes, LPG, electricity, and sustainable woodlots.
A Balanced View: Livelihoods vs. Sustainability

The Case for Enforcement: Environmental advocates and officials argue that unchecked charcoal trade undermines national reforestation goals, National Forestry Authority mandates, and UgandaÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂs international climate commitments. Short-term arrests and seizures aim to deter large-scale commercial operators who exploit forests for profit, often evading licenses or operating in protected areas. Public support for reporting illegal activities is seen as key to community-owned conservation.

Challenges and Human Impact: Charcoal remains a critical energy source and income generator for thousands, especially in regions with limited alternatives. Rural producers, transporters, and tradersÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂoften operating at subsistence levelsÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂmay view the ban as disruptive to their livelihoods. Critics sometimes point to uneven enforcement, alleged corruption in some checkpoints, or the need for stronger support systems (e.g., alternative income programs, subsidized clean energy, or regulated sustainable charcoal from planted forests). Effective policy must balance ecological protection with socio-economic realities to avoid driving activities underground or exacerbating poverty.

Past operations have shown mixed results: temporary reductions in trade followed by resurgence when enforcement wanes. Long-term success likely requires investment in alternatives, community forestry management, and stricter licensing for any permitted production.Looking ForwardThe arrest of these eight suspects in West Nile is part of a larger narrative of government resolve on environmental governance. As operations continue, outcomes will depend on prosecution rates, deterrence effect, and complementary initiatives that offer viable pathways away from destructive practices.For West Nile and Northern Uganda, the stakes are high: healthy forests mean better rainfall patterns, fertile soils, and resilient communities. Sustainable energy transitions are no longer optional but essential for the regionÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂs future.King Musah Media calls for transparent enforcement, community engagement, and practical alternatives to ensure environmental protection benefits rather than burdens the people it seeks to safeguard.

A Ugandan at the helm of the UN would be historic and symbolically powerful for Africa. title: National Cleaning Day: A Bold National Initiative Marred by Coercion and Controversy
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Uganda's inaugural National Cleaning Day drew praise for civic mobilisation but sharp criticism after videos showed police using roadblocks and force to enforce participation.
image_alt: Community members cleaning a street with brooms and shovels
content: On Saturday, July 25, 2026, Uganda rolled out its inaugural National Cleaning Day, a government-mandated initiative designating the last Saturday of every month from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. for nationwide cleanup. Branded under the slogan "A Clean Uganda Is Everybody's Responsibility", the programme aims to tackle poor sanitation, curb disease outbreaks like cholera, and foster environmental stewardship.

Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja and other officials led activities in Kisenyi, Kampala, where communities, local leaders, and residents turned out with shovels, brooms, and good intentions. Many Ugandans embraced the day, viewing it as a practical step toward healthier neighbourhoods, and in principle a structured, collective effort to instill discipline and shared responsibility deserves praise after decades of rapid urbanisation and weak waste management have turned parts of Kampala into breeding grounds for preventable illness.

A different, more troubling story. Videos and eyewitness accounts quickly surfaced showing police enforcing the directive with roadblocks, spikes, and physical force. In one widely circulated clip, religious leaders in clerical attire were halted at a blockade, unable to proceed as police asserted that "no one is above the law." Another video, shared by opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi (Bobi Wine), depicted security personnel manhandling a young man in a public area apparently for non-compliance raising questions about proportionality during what should have been a community exercise.

Bobi Wine condemned the approach: "The Ugandan regime at it again! Now using force and violence to enforce a 'cleaning campaign'! Again, they've lost any ability to persuade so they have to coerce." His criticism resonates with broader frustrations over the timing and rigidity of the exercise, particularly its impact on weekend economic activities, religious services, and vulnerable informal workers who rely on daily earnings. Critics also point out selective enforcement, with powerful individuals or vehicles often bypassing restrictions that ensnare ordinary citizens.

A balanced reckoning. The government deserves credit for prioritising sanitation as a national priority poor waste management costs lives and productivity annually, and mobilising citizens can build civic pride when done right. However, a campaign promoting collective responsibility loses moral authority when implemented through heavy-handed policing that alienates the very people it seeks to engage. Moving forward, authorities should refine the initiative: provide advance public education, exempt critical religious and emergency movements, invest in waste infrastructure, and emphasise voluntary participation backed by incentives.

Uganda's streets, markets, and drainages desperately need cleaning not just on designated Saturdays, but every day. The question is whether National Cleaning Day evolves into genuine nation-building or remains another top-down exercise that divides more than it unites. King Musah Media will continue tracking implementation across regions.

title: Muwanga Kivumbi: Two Weeks of Silence After Televised Abduction Where Is the Rule of Law?
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Sixteen days after his interception at a Mpigi roadblock, Muwanga Kivumbi's whereabouts remain officially unknown, as police deny holding him and a habeas corpus process unfolds.
image_alt: A radio studio microphone setup
content: More than two weeks after Hon. Muhammad Muwanga Kivumbi National Unity Platform Vice President for Buganda and former Butambala MP was reportedly intercepted at a roadblock in Mpigi shortly after being granted bail, his whereabouts remain officially unknown to the public. Police have denied holding him, even as a High Court habeas corpus process unfolds and serious concerns about his safety and health mount.

This is not a routine arrest. It is a high-profile case involving a sitting political figure who had just secured judicial release on terrorism-related charges linked to post-election violence. The optics interception soon after bail, followed by official silence fuel legitimate fears of enforced disappearance, a tactic increasingly associated with Uganda's security apparatus.

A senior officer weighs in. In a widely circulated radio interview on Radio 4/103.3 FM, Lt. Gen. Proscovia Nalweyiso, a senior military officer, addressed the Kivumbi matter directly. Her tone was firm: she defended the actions of security forces and suggested that Kivumbi's outspoken criticism and political conduct have predictable consequences. While acknowledging freedom of expression, she essentially argued that it is not unlimited particularly when it challenges established authority or borders on what authorities deem destabilising.

The contradictions are stark. Authorities have publicly stated they do not know Kivumbi's location, despite the highly visible nature of his interception. The case remains active in the judicial system, with bail previously granted, yet the executive arm of government appears to operate with a parallel reality. This episode fits a worrying template: arrests of opposition figures, releases on bail, followed by re-arrests or disappearances, often justified on vague national security grounds.

Kivumbi is no ordinary citizen he has made sharp criticisms of the government, including President Museveni, the First Family, and security institutions. If credible evidence links him to violence or other crimes, he must face justice through transparent courts, not shadowy roadblocks and unexplained custody. Nalweyiso's point on the limits of expression cannot be entirely dismissed in theory, but Uganda's security agencies have repeatedly been accused of overreach, with political opponents disproportionately targeted.

Hon. Muwanga Kivumbi must be produced in court or accounted for immediately. Sixteen days is too long. The courts, the police, and the military must choose: uphold the Constitution for all citizens, or confirm the growing perception that in Uganda, power still trumps law. King Musah Media demands answers not for Kivumbi alone, but for the principle that no Ugandan should vanish into the system without trace.

title: Muhoozi in Kigali: Military Diplomacy or Succession Signal Amid Domestic Shadows?
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba's two-day working visit to Kigali showcases regional military diplomacy, even as domestic concerns over abductions and succession politics intensify.
image_alt: Military officials shaking hands at a formal diplomatic reception
content: Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Chief of Defence Forces of the Uganda Peoples' Defence Forces, arrived in Kigali on Saturday, July 25, 2026, for a two-day official working visit. He was received by his Rwandan counterpart, Gen. Mubarakh Muganga, Chief of Defence Staff of the Rwanda Defence Force, and is scheduled to hold high-level talks, including a meeting with President Paul Kagame.

Official statements from both sides describe the visit as focused on deepening military cooperation, bilateral ties, and regional peace and security standard fare for neighbourly military diplomacy between two nations that have had a complex, sometimes tense relationship now apparently on the mend.

The positive case. Supporters of Gen. Muhoozi view such visits as evidence of a confident, outward-looking leader building the international relationships necessary for Uganda's stability. Rwanda and Uganda share borders, security concerns, and economic interests, and strengthening military-to-military ties can help prevent misunderstandings that plagued the two countries in the past.

The domestic cloud. Yet this polished regional diplomacy contrasts sharply with growing unease inside Uganda. Gen. Muhoozi has, in recent years, issued blunt public statements many Ugandans interpret as direct threats warnings about "switching off" critical media outlets, references to abductions, and strong rhetoric against opposition figures. The unresolved case of Hon. Muwanga Kivumbi arrested, granted bail, then re-arrested and missing for over two weeks adds to the anxiety, even though authorities have not officially linked Muhoozi to specific disappearances.

At the heart of the national conversation is the succession question. President Yoweri Museveni, now in his 80s and having ruled Uganda for over 40 years, shows no public intention of stepping aside, and many Ugandans quietly assume Gen. Muhoozi is being positioned as the eventual successor. Critics argue this dynastic perception undermines democratic development and question whether his regional engagements are genuine diplomacy or an attempt to burnish international credentials ahead of a future leadership bid.

Gen. Muhoozi's visit to Rwanda is legitimate state business that serves Uganda's national interest if it produces real security and economic cooperation. But a leader who projects strength abroad must also demonstrate respect for constitutionalism, rule of law, and civil liberties at home. King Musah Media will continue to report developments from Kigali and Kampala without fear or favour.

title: Erias Lukwago's Bail Bid: Health Crisis or High-Stakes Political Chess?
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The High Court is set to rule on Erias Lukwago's bail application on July 30, as his legal team cites a litany of serious health conditions worsened by prolonged detention.
image_alt: A hospital bed in a quiet ward
content: Former Kampala Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago remains in Luzira Prison, with the High Court Criminal Division set to rule on his bail application on July 30, 2026. Justice David Matovu presided over proceedings where Lukwago, charged with misprision of treason, sought release primarily on health grounds. His legal team presented a litany of conditions: hypertension, chronic gastritis, hiatus hernia, tinnitus, serious spinal complications, respiratory issues, and post-operative complications requiring specialised care unavailable in prison.

Court records show he was briefly transferred to Mulago National Referral Hospital on June 25 on medical recommendation, yet doctors reportedly struggled to manage his deteriorating state. Lukwago's lawyers secured a production warrant, but the core argument centres on humanity versus security: can the state justify detaining a man whose health is visibly failing while he awaits trial?

The charges and context. Prosecution alleges that between 2021 and November 2024, in Kampala, Geneva, and Nairobi, Lukwago knew of a treasonous plot involving Dr. Kizza Besigye and others but failed to report it an offence under Section 25 of the Penal Code Act. Lukwago and his supporters dismiss this as politically motivated persecution aimed at silencing a vocal opposition figure. This case fits a familiar pattern in Uganda's polarised politics: high-profile arrests, lengthy pre-trial detention, and repeated bail battles.

The human element. Videos and statements circulating from Lukwago's camp paint a picture of a man fighting serious illness, prompting strong reactions even from parody and activist accounts. At the same time, courts must balance individual rights against the gravity of charges if evidence of treason involvement holds weight, release on bail could pose risks. Yet prolonged detention without speedy trial, especially amid documented health decline, risks turning justice into punishment by default.

Uganda's courts have occasionally granted bail in politically sensitive cases, but consistency remains elusive. The forthcoming July 30 ruling will signal whether the judiciary prioritises medical evidence and humane considerations or leans toward prolonged incarceration amid serious allegations. King Musah Media will monitor the ruling closely justice must not only be done but must be seen to be done.

title: Karamoja Hunger Crisis: Emergency Relief Meets Accusations of Neglect and Exploitation
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: As government and WFP roll out emergency food relief in Karamoja, critics accuse a high-profile land initiative of diverting harvests away from the very communities it promised to feed.
image_alt: A dry, cracked landscape typical of drought conditions
content: As Uganda observed its inaugural National Cleaning Day, a more sobering reality unfolded in the northeast: Karamoja is once again gripped by severe drought-induced hunger. The sub-region, long one of Uganda's most vulnerable, is witnessing acute food shortages affecting thousands, with women and children bearing the heaviest burden.

Government and humanitarian response. The Office of the Prime Minister, working with partners including the World Food Programme, has rolled out emergency food distribution across multiple districts, including Moroto and Napak. Ministers Sam Engola and John Baptist Lokii have been on the ground overseeing operations, part of a government commitment backed by UGX 45 billion for immediate relief. WFP Country Director Wanja Kaaria reaffirmed support for the government's efforts, emphasising a shift from short-term handouts toward long-term resilience, including school feeding, nutrition programmes, and plans for national grain silos.

Sharp criticisms. The response has not silenced critics who argue the crisis was foreseeable. A prominent pastor's "Bucket Initiative," which reportedly raised billions to feed over a million people, faces pointed questions from local voices who accuse the ministry of acquiring land in Karamoja under the promise of agricultural transformation, only for sorghum to be harvested and reportedly supplied to breweries in Kampala. Commentators also point to decades of marginalisation, land grabbing allegations, and inadequate investment in irrigation and sustainable agriculture.

Balanced assessment. Managing Karamoja's challenges is complex historical cattle rustling, harsh climate, and socio-cultural factors complicate development, and the current relief effort shows responsiveness. But the recurring nature of Karamoja crises points to deeper policy and governance failures, and when large-scale land allocations to outsiders coincide with local hunger, public scepticism is understandable and demands transparent accountability.

No political spin changes the fact that children in Karamoja are going to bed hungry today. Emergency food is a bandage; sustainable solutions irrigation, genuine community land rights, market access, and climate adaptation are the cure. King Musah Media will keep following developments in Karamoja.

title: Gen. Moses Ali Laid to Rest in Adjumani: A Nation Bids Farewell to a Veteran Statesman
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Gen. Moses Ali has been laid to rest at his ancestral home in Adjumani, closing days of national mourning that included a lying-in-state at Parliament and tributes from President Museveni.
image_alt: Mourners gathered at a burial ceremony in Adjumani
content: The late Gen. (Rtd) Hon. Moses Ali, former Second Deputy Prime Minister and one of Uganda's longest-serving public servants, has been laid to rest at his ancestral home in Adjumani District after an emotional farewell that drew leaders, military officials, family, and thousands of mourners from across the country.

The burial on Wednesday, July 23, 2026, marked the end of several days of national mourning that included Janaza prayers in Kampala, a lying-in-state at Parliament, and a special gathering at Paridi Stadium in Adjumani.

Final journey and ceremony. Mourners gathered at Paridi Stadium in the morning for a special ceremony involving representatives from the 15 districts of West Nile. This was followed by Janaza prayers at Abirichaku before the burial at 4:00 PM. The solemn event brought together dignitaries, military personnel, and local communities to honour a man widely respected for his humility, service, and dedication to his people.

Presidential condolence message. In a special message, President Yoweri Museveni praised the late Gen. Ali as a passionate advocate who deeply cared for his people and contributed immensely to the nation's development, especially in the West Nile region. Earlier tributes in Parliament highlighted Ali's sense of humour, humility, and commitment to public service, with Leader of Opposition Joel Ssenyonyi, Hon. Betty Nambooze, Minister Balaam Barugahara, and others remembering him fondly as a true patriot and "man of the people."

A remarkable legacy. Born in 1939, Gen. Moses Ali rose through the ranks as a military officer, lawyer, and politician. He served in multiple high-level roles, including as Second Deputy Prime Minister and MP for Adjumani West until his passing on July 18, 2026, at Nakasero Hospital at the age of 87. His death has prompted an outpouring of respect from across the political spectrum, underscoring his role as a unifying figure who served Uganda with distinction for over five decades.

As the body of the veteran leader now rests in his ancestral soil, King Musah Media joins the nation in mourning this great loss. May the soul of Gen. Hon. Moses Ali rest in eternal peace. Farewell to a true son of Uganda.

title: Court Gives Security Agencies 3 Days to Account for Missing Muwanga Kivumbi Amid Mounting Pressure and Rumours
author: Musanya Musa
excerpt: High Court Justice Collins Acellam orders the CDF and IGP to report within three days on Muwanga Kivumbi's whereabouts, as unconfirmed rumours of torture continue to swirl.
image_alt: The exterior of the High Court of Uganda
content: In a significant judicial intervention, High Court Justice Collins Acellam has ordered the Chief of Defence Forces and the Inspector General of Police to report within three days on the whereabouts and circumstances surrounding the continued detention of Hon. Muhammad Muwanga Kivumbi. The directive comes as speculation intensifies over the NUP leader's fate more than ten days after his abduction.

This development marks a critical escalation in efforts to pierce the veil of silence that has enveloped Kivumbi since July 10, underscoring growing institutional pushback against opaque security operations while highlighting the limits of executive impunity in the face of judicial scrutiny.

Judicial demand for answers. Justice Acellam's order requires security chiefs to clarify Kivumbi's location, the agency holding him, and the legal basis for his detention. The move responds to persistent concerns raised in habeas corpus applications and parliamentary queries. Kivumbi's lawyers have long argued that his incommunicado status violates constitutional protections, including the right to be produced in court within 48 hours.

The ruling arrives against a backdrop of unconfirmed but persistent rumours amplified on social media and in opposition circles alleging torture, severe injury, or even death. While no credible evidence has substantiated the most extreme claims, the absence of official information has understandably fuelled public anxiety and distrust.

The abduction and its aftermath. Kivumbi was granted bail by the International Crimes Division on July 9 after 169 days on remand over terrorism charges linked to Butambala post-election violence. Hours later, on July 10, armed operatives including men in uniform intercepted him at a Mpigi roadblock in a coordinated operation involving police and plainclothes personnel. He was bundled into an unmarked vehicle and has not been publicly seen or heard from since. Family-organised prayers in Butambala drew senior opposition figures, and NUP leader Bobi Wine has publicly cited reports of torture at a military facility and demanded accountability.

The imperative of transparency. Investigations into serious allegations like terrorism require diligence. However, when court bail is swiftly followed by extra-judicial action and prolonged secrecy, it invites accusations of lawfare and abuse of power. The three-day clock is ticking, and Ugandans deserve closure on whether Kivumbi is alive and well, facing legitimate charges through due process, or has once again seen the state prioritise control over constitutional norms. Justice Acellam's order is a welcome assertion of judicial authority; the nation awaits the response.

title: Body of Gen. Moses Ali Flown to Adjumani as Parliament Pays Glowing Tributes
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: President Museveni and Parliament pay emotional tribute to Gen. Moses Ali as his body is airlifted to Adjumani, ahead of burial tomorrow, Wednesday July 23.
image_alt: Parliament in session with dignitaries paying tribute
content: Emotional tributes poured in at Parliament today as the body of veteran statesman Gen. Hon. Moses Ali lay in state, before being airlifted to Adjumani District ahead of his burial tomorrow, Wednesday, July 23, 2026.

The special parliamentary session formed the climax of the day's programme, honouring a man who served Uganda for over five decades as a soldier, lawyer, minister, and legislator. President Yoweri Museveni, Speaker Anita Among, Leader of Opposition Joel Ssenyonyi, Minister Balaam Barugahara, Hon. Betty Nambooze, Speaker-designate Oboth Oboth Jacob, and many others paid heartfelt respects.

President Museveni's tribute. President Museveni, who laid a wreath on the casket, recalled Gen. Ali's courageous history. "I was the first man to oppose Idi Amin," the President stated, highlighting Ali's early resistance and long service to the nation.

Parliamentary tributes. Leader of Opposition Joel Ssenyonyi honoured Gen. Ali's five decades of public service while using the occasion to raise concerns about the rule of law, abductions, and unlawful detentions, urging the President to rein in security agencies. Hon. Betty Nambooze remembered Gen. Ali's humility, recalling the day she contested for Speaker against him and noting that despite the competition, he remained respectful and a true "man of the people." Speaker Oboth Oboth recalled Gen. Ali's sense of humour and love for joking, lightening the mood even in serious moments, while Minister Balaam Barugahara and other leaders also delivered moving tributes praising his dedication and legacy.
The tributes painted a picture of Gen. Ali as a principled, humorous, and resilient statesman who bridged divides and served with distinction across different regimes.

Journey to final rest. Following the parliamentary session and ceremony at Kololo Airstrip, the body was airlifted to the West Nile region and has now arrived in Adjumani, where it will spend the night before the final rites tomorrow. Wednesday's programme includes a special gathering at Paridi Stadium in the morning involving the 15 districts of West Nile, Janaza prayer at Abirichaku at 3:00 PM, and burial at his ancestral home at 4:00 PM.

Born in 1939, Gen. Moses Ali served as Second Deputy Prime Minister, MP for Adjumani West, and held several other senior positions. His death at Nakasero Hospital on July 18 has left a significant void in Uganda's political landscape, particularly in the West Nile sub-region. As the nation bids farewell, King Musah Media extends deepest condolences to the family, the people of Adjumani, and all who knew and worked with this remarkable leader. May his soul rest in eternal peace. King Musah Media will continue to bring you live updates from Adjumani tomorrow.

title: Where is Hon. Muwanga Kivumbi? Rumours of Death and Torture Swirl as Abduction Enters Second Week
author: Musanya Musa
excerpt: More than ten days after his re-arrest hours following a court-granted bail, Muwanga Kivumbi's whereabouts remain unknown, fuelling unverified rumours of torture and death.
image_alt: A group gathered for prayers in solidarity
content: More than ten days after his dramatic re-arrest, the whereabouts of Hon. Muhammad Muwanga Kivumbi, former Butambala County MP and NUP Deputy President for Buganda, remain unknown to his family, lawyers, and the public. This silence has fuelled disturbing rumours: that he was killed, tortured to death, or is receiving treatment in hospital after severe abuse. These claims, while unverified, cannot be dismissed lightly in a context where enforced disappearances and incommunicado detention have become disturbingly familiar.

The abduction in broad daylight. On July 9, 2026, Justice Susan Okalanyi granted Kivumbi bail after 169 days on remand over terrorism charges tied to post-election violence in Butambala. The following day, while travelling from Butambala toward Kampala, his vehicle was intercepted at a roadblock in Mpigi. Eyewitnesses and video evidence show traffic police involvement, followed by armed men ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ some in UPDF uniforms with face coverings, others in plainclothes ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ who surrounded the car, pulled him out, and bundled him into an unmarked "drone" vehicle. Attempts by supporters and journalists to follow were blocked. This occurred mere hours after a court-ordered release, raising profound questions about respect for judicial authority.

Circulating reports and public anguish. Disturbing allegations have proliferated on social media and in opposition circles. NUP leader Robert Kyagulanyi (Bobi Wine) highlighted reports that Kivumbi "was tortured to near death at Kasenyi SFC military barracks and is now being hidden from the public while receiving treatment before he can be produced." Kivumbi's family organised dua (Islamic prayers) in Butambala, attended by Leader of the Opposition Hon. Joel Ssenyonyi, NUP Acting President Hon. John Baptist Nambeshe, and other political figures ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ a public show of solidarity and quiet desperation. No official confirmation of death, torture, or hospitalisation has emerged from authorities.

A pattern of abductions. Kivumbi's case does not exist in isolation. Uganda has witnessed multiple high-profile instances of opposition figures, activists, and civilians being picked up by security operatives ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ often in unmarked vehicles ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ and held without immediate judicial oversight. The Uganda Law Society and human rights advocates have repeatedly condemned such practices as erosions of constitutional protections. Habeas corpus applications, like the one filed by Kivumbi's lawyers naming the CDF, IGP, and Attorney General, seek exactly this clarity: produce him dead or alive, or release him.

Where is Hon. Muwanga Kivumbi? After more than ten days, the burden lies squarely on state agencies to account for his well-being and legal status. Rumours of death or critical injury thrive in information vacuums; transparency is the antidote. The prayers in Butambala and public outcry reflect not just concern for one man, but for the soul of constitutional governance.

title: AK47's Widow Nalongo Maggie Kaweesi Passes Away at Mengo Hospital
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Nalongo Maggie Kaweesi, widow of late dancehall artist AK47 and mother of his twins, has died at Mengo Hospital after battling sickle cell disease.
image_alt: A hospital ward corridor
content: Nalongo Maggie Kaweesi, the widow of the late Ugandan dancehall artist Emmanuel Mayanja, popularly known as AK47, and mother of his twins, has died.

According to family sources and close associates, Maggie was first admitted at Nsambya Hospital after falling ill. She was later referred to Mengo Hospital for further management, where she sadly passed away on Monday, July 20, 2026.
Maggie had been battling sickle cell disease for some time, and her condition reportedly worsened after she returned to Uganda from abroad. She leaves behind the twins she had with the late AK47.

The news has shocked the Ugandan entertainment industry, with many artists and fans sending condolences to the Mayanja family and the children who have now lost both parents. Funeral arrangements are yet to be announced by the family. May her soul rest in eternal peace.

title: Nnamwandu w'eyali omuyimbi omugenzi AK47, Nnaalongo Maggie Kaweesi afudde
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: Nalongo Maggie Kaweesi, nnamwandu w'omuyimbi AK47, afiiridde mu ddwaliro e Mengo ng'alwadde sickle cell.
image_alt: Ekifo ky'eddwaliro
content: Nalongo Maggie Kaweesi afiridde mu ddwaliro ly'e Mengo akawungezi ke gulo nga ono ye yali mukazi w'omugenzi Emmanuel Mayanja eyali amanyiddwa ennyo nga AK47.
Okusinziira ku bolugandabe n'abamumanyi, Maggie yasooka kujjanjabwa mu Nsambya Hospital oluvannyuma natwalibwa mu Mengo Hospital mwe yafiiridde ku balaza ya wiiki eno nga, July 20, 2026.
Maggie abadde atawanyizibwa omusujja gwa nalubiri "sickle cell" era embeera ye yeyongera okwononeka oluvannyuma lw'okudda mu Uganda ng'ava ebweru.
Famire ya Ba Mayanja nabakungubazi abalalaba balabiddwako mu ddwaliro e mengo wabula nga entekateeka zokuziika tezinaba kufulumizibwa. Omwoyo gwomugenzi Mukama agulamuze kisa.

title: High Court to Hear Erias Lukwago Bail Application on July 24 Amid Health Concerns and Treason-Related Charges
author: King Musah Media News Desk
excerpt: The High Court will hear Erias Lukwago's bail application on July 24, as a Mulago medical report details serious chronic conditions worsened during his remand.

content: The High Court in Kampala has scheduled July 24, 2026, to hear the bail application of former Kampala Lord Mayor and senior lawyer Erias Lukwago, who faces charges of misprision of treason. The case revolves around allegations that between 2021 and November 2024, Lukwago had knowledge of an alleged plot involving his clients ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ including Dr. Kizza Besigye and Hajji Obeid Lutale Kamulegeya ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ to overthrow the government but failed to report it or take preventive steps.

Lukwago, a vocal opposition figure and president of the People's Front for Freedom, denies the charges. As Besigye's lawyer, he has been central to high-profile political cases, adding layers of scrutiny to his own prosecution. His situation intersects with the re-arrest of figures like Muwanga Kivumbi, reflecting broader security operations targeting perceived threats.

Health deterioration and Mulago report. Lukwago's remand has been marked by serious health complications. Following his arrest on June 15, 2026, reports emerged of a hypertension crisis (readings reportedly reaching 217/100) and aggravated spinal issues. He was transferred to Mulago National Referral Hospital after a court order, where a panel of senior consultants assessed him. The Mulago medical report confirms multiple chronic conditions: well-controlled hypertension, unresolved post-COVID-19 lung disease with mild bronchiectasis, persistent tinnitus and loss of smell, residual cervical radiculitis post-spinal surgery in India, and non-erosive gastroesophageal reflux disease with hiatus hernia.

Doctors recommended continued medication, a well-ventilated environment, ongoing ear treatment, and potential further evaluation by his Indian spine surgeons. Lukwago has remained frail, in pain, and under treatment, with his legal team describing him as weak while praising Mulago's care within its capacity; plans for possible transfer abroad for specialised care have been discussed.

Bold questions on procedure. Lukwago's arrest and initial detention sparked controversy over the manner of handling a senior advocate and former elected leader, which his lawyers say contributed directly to his medical distress.
